Let the pork chops rest for 5 minutes before serving. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the finished dish before serving.

title: Pan-Seared Rosemary Pork Chops with Roasted Asparagus and Sweet Potato
ingredients_json: ["300 g Pork chop, boneless, lean", "300 g Sweet potato", "250 g Asparagus, fresh", "30 ml Olive oil", "10 g Garlic, cloves", "2 g Rosemary, fresh", "3 g Salt", "0.5 g Black pepper, ground", "50 g Lemon, fresh"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Wash the asparagus and trim the woody ends. In a medium bowl, toss the sweet potato with 10 ml of olive oil, 1.5 g of salt, and 0.25 g of black pepper. Spread the sweet potato cubes in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes, then add the asparagus to the same baking sheet, toss lightly with the sweet potato, and continue roasting for another 10-15 minutes, or until the sweet potato is tender and the asparagus is crisp-tender. While the vegetables are roasting, prepare the pork chops. Mince the garlic and finely chop the fresh rosemary. Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels. Season both sides of the pork chops with the remaining 1.5 g of salt and 0.25 g of black pepper. Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat with the remaining 20 ml of olive oil. Once hot, sear the pork chops for 3-4 minutes per side until beautifully browned. Add the minced garlic and chopped rosemary to the pan during the last minute of searing, being careful not to burn the garlic. Transfer the skillet with the pork chops to the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove the pork chops from the oven, squeeze fresh lemon juice over them, and let them rest for 5 minutes before serving with the roasted sweet potato and asparagus.

title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Roasted Root Vegetables and Spiced Apple
ingredients_json: ["300 g Pork chop, loin, lean, raw", "200 g Carrot, raw", "150 g Parsnip, raw", "200 g Sweet potato, raw", "180 g Apple, raw, with skin", "30 ml Olive oil", "2 g Thyme, dried", "1.5 g Garlic powder", "1.5 g Paprika, ground", "3 g Salt, table", "1 g Black pepper, ground", "15 ml Apple cider vinegar"]
instructions:
Preheat your oven to 200 degrees Celsius. Wash and peel the carrots, parsnips, and sweet potato, then chop them into even, bite-sized pieces. Core the apple and cut it into similar-sized wedges, leaving the skin on. In a large bowl, combine the chopped root vegetables and apple with 20 ml of the olive oil, dried thyme, garlic powder, paprika, half of the salt, and half of the black pepper, tossing until everything is well coated. Spread the seasoned vegetables and apple in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized, flipping halfway through.

While the vegetables are roasting, pat the pork chops dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with the remaining salt and black pepper. Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat with the remaining 10 ml of olive oil. Once the oil is shimmering, carefully place the pork chops in the skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until a deep golden-brown crust forms. If your pork chops are thick (over 2.5 cm), you may transfer the skillet to the oven with the vegetables for the last 5-10 minutes of their roasting time, or until the internal temperature of the pork reaches 63 degrees Celsius. Remove the chops from the skillet and let them rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Deglaze the skillet by adding the apple cider vinegar and scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Let it simmer for 1-2 minutes until slightly reduced. Serve the pan-seared pork chops alongside the roasted root vegetables and spiced apple, drizzling with the pan sauce.

title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Rosemary Sweet Potato Mash and Roasted Asparagus
ingredients_json: ["2 pieces Pork loin chop, boneless, lean", "400 g Sweet potato, raw", "250 g Asparagus, raw", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "2 cloves Garlic, raw", "5 g Rosemary, fresh", "3 g Salt", "1 g Black pepper", "50 ml Chicken stock, low sodium"]
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Wash and peel the sweet potatoes, then cut them into 2 cm cubes. Place them in a pot with enough water to cover, bring to a boil, and cook for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain the sweet potatoes and mash them with a fork, incorporating 1 tablespoon of olive oil, 1.5 grams of salt, and 0.5 grams of black pepper. Keep warm. While the sweet potatoes are cooking, trim the woody ends off the asparagus spears. In a bowl, toss the asparagus with 0.5 tablespoon of olive oil, 0.5 gram of salt, and 0.25 gram of black pepper. Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp. Meanwhile, mince the garlic and finely chop the fresh rosemary. Pat the pork chops dry with paper towels. Season both sides with the remaining 1 gram of salt and 0.25 gram of black pepper. Heat the remaining 0.5 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the pork chops and sear for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature of 63°C). Remove the chops from the skillet and let them rest on a plate. Deglaze the skillet with the chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 1-2 minutes until slightly reduced. Serve the pan-seared pork chops alongside the rosemary sweet potato mash and roasted asparagus, drizzling the pan sauce over the chops.

title: Herb-Roasted Pork Shoulder with Sweet Potatoes and Green Beans
ingredients_json: ["1.2 kg Pork shoulder, boneless, lean", "800 g Sweet potato, raw, with skin", "400 g Green beans, fresh", "200 g Onion, yellow, raw", "20 g Garlic, raw", "30 ml Olive oil, extra virgin", "10 g Rosemary, fresh", "5 g Thyme, fresh", "6 g Salt, table", "3 g Black pepper, ground", "250 ml Chicken broth, low sodium"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Pat the pork shoulder dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, finely chopped rosemary, thyme, salt, and black pepper to create a rub. Generously apply the herb rub all over the pork shoulder, ensuring it's evenly coated. Peel and chop the sweet potatoes and onion into large, uniform chunks. Mince the garlic cloves. In a large roasting pan, place the pork shoulder in the center. Arrange the chopped sweet potatoes and onions around the pork. Pour the low sodium chicken broth into the bottom of the pan. Roast for 2 hours, then add the fresh green beans to the pan, tossing them with the other vegetables. Continue roasting for another 30-45 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for medium-rare, or higher for desired doneness, and the vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized. Remove the pork from the oven, tent it loosely with foil, and let it rest for 15 minutes before slicing. Serve the sliced pork with the roasted sweet potatoes, onions, and green beans, drizzling with any pan juices.

title: Slow-Braised Pork Shoulder with Root Vegetables and Herbs
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Pork shoulder, boneless, lean", "15 ml Olive oil", "200 g Onion, yellow, raw", "300 g Carrot, raw", "150 g Celery stalk, raw", "500 g Potato, raw, russet", "500 ml Chicken broth, low sodium", "200 ml Crushed tomatoes, canned", "5 g Garlic clove, raw", "5 g Salt, table", "2 g Black pepper, ground", "10 g Rosemary, fresh", "10 g Thyme, fresh"]
instructions: Start by patting the pork shoulder dry with paper towels. Season generously all over with salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear the pork shoulder on all sides until deeply browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the pork from the pot and set aside. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the chopped onions, carrots, and celery to the pot and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Mince the garlic and add it to the vegetables, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Pour in the chicken broth and crushed tomatoes, bringing the mixture to a simmer. Return the seared pork shoulder to the pot. Add the fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs, submerging them partially in the liquid. If needed, add a little more broth to ensure the pork is at least halfway submerged. Bring back to a gentle simmer, then cover the pot tightly and transfer it to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5 hours. After 2.5 hours, add the diced potatoes to the pot, ensuring they are mostly submerged in the liquid. Continue braising, covered, for another 1 to 1.5 hours, or until the pork is fork-tender and the vegetables are soft. Remove the pot from the oven, skim off any excess fat from the surface of the sauce, and remove the herb sprigs. Shred the pork directly in the pot with two forks, mixing it into the sauce and vegetables. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary before serving hot.

title: Slow-Cooked Pork Shoulder with Root Vegetables and Apples
ingredients_json: ["600 g Pork shoulder, boneless, trimmed", "15 ml Olive oil", "200 g Onion, yellow, raw", "3 cloves Garlic, raw", "300 g Carrots, raw", "250 g Sweet potato, raw", "200 g Parsnip, raw", "2 piece Apple, medium, raw", "500 ml Chicken broth, low sodium", "30 ml Apple cider vinegar", "3 sprigs Rosemary, fresh", "4 sprigs Thyme, fresh", "1 piece Bay leaf, dried", "5 g Salt", "2 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Pat the pork shoulder dry thoroughly with paper towels and season generously on all sides with salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place the seasoned pork in the hot pot and sear it on all sides until deeply browned, which should take about 5-7 minutes total. Remove the pork from the pot and set it aside on a plate. Reduce the heat to medium, then add the chopped onion to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it. Deglaze the pot by pouring in the apple cider vinegar and scraping up any browned bits from the bottom with a wooden spoon. Pour in the chicken broth and bring it to a gentle simmer. Return the seared pork to the pot. Add the chopped carrots, sweet potatoes, and parsnips around the pork. Tuck in the fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs, and the bay leaf. Cover the pot tightly with its lid and transfer it to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until the pork is exceptionally tender and easily shreds with a fork. About 30 minutes before the end of the cooking time, stir in the chopped apples. Once cooked, carefully remove the pork from the pot and place it on a cutting board. Using two forks, shred the pork into bite-sized pieces. Discard the bay leaf and herb sprigs from the pot. Return the shredded pork to the pot with the cooked vegetables and apples, tossing gently to combine all the ingredients with the flavorful sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve warm, directly from the pot.

title: Slow-Cooked Pork Shoulder with Root Vegetables and Apple Cider Glaze
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Pork shoulder, boneless, lean", "15 ml Olive oil", "10 g Salt", "2 g Black pepper, ground", "1 piece Onion, raw", "500 g Carrot, raw", "300 g Parsnip, raw", "2 g Dried thyme", "2 dl Apple cider, unsweetened"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C. Pat the pork shoulder dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear the pork on all sides until nicely browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the pork and set aside. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and parsnips to the pot and sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened. Stir in the dried thyme. Deglaze the pot with apple cider, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Return the pork shoulder to the pot. Cover tightly and transfer to the preheated oven. Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until the pork is very tender and easily shreds with a fork. Remove the pork from the pot and let it rest on a cutting board for 10 minutes before shredding. While the pork rests, skim any excess fat from the cooking liquid. Reduce the liquid over medium-high heat on the stovetop for 5-10 minutes until it slightly thickens into a glaze. Serve the shredded pork and roasted vegetables with the apple cider glaze.

title: Herb-Crusted Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Root Vegetables and Broccoli
ingredients_json: ["500 g Pork tenderloin, raw", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "4 cloves Garlic, raw, unpeeled", "10 g Thyme, fresh", "5 g Rosemary, fresh", "5 g Salt, table", "2 g Pepper, black, ground", "300 g Carrots, raw", "300 g Parsnips, raw", "150 g Onion, red, raw", "400 g Broccoli, raw", "0.5 piece Lemon, raw"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Begin by preparing the herb crust for the pork tenderloin; in a small bowl, finely mince the garlic, chop the fresh thyme and rosemary, then combine them with 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Season the pork tenderloin generously all over with salt and black pepper, then rub the herb mixture evenly onto its surface. Next, prepare the root vegetables: peel and chop the carrots and parsnips into roughly 2 cm pieces, and peel and quarter the red onion. Toss these chopped vegetables with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper on a large baking sheet, spreading them into a single layer. Place the baking sheet with the root vegetables into the preheated oven and roast for 15 minutes. While the vegetables are roasting, wash and cut the broccoli into florets. After the initial 15 minutes of roasting, carefully add the herb-crusted pork tenderloin to the baking sheet alongside the partially cooked root vegetables. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the pork reaches 63°C when measured with a meat thermometer. Add the broccoli florets to the baking sheet for the last 10 minutes of cooking, ensuring they are tender-crisp. Once the pork is cooked, remove the baking sheet from the oven and transfer the pork tenderloin to a cutting board, loosely tenting it with foil, to rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing. Slice the rested pork tenderloin into medallions and serve immediately with the roasted root vegetables and broccoli, finishing with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice over the entire dish.

title: Herb-Roasted Pork Tenderloin with Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["500 g Pork tenderloin, raw", "300 g Carrot, raw", "300 g Parsnip, raw", "300 g Potato, raw", "30 ml Olive oil", "3 piece Garlic, raw", "15 ml Rosemary, fresh, chopped", "15 ml Thyme, fresh, chopped", "5 g Salt, table", "2 g Black pepper, ground", "100 g Green beans, raw"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Peel and chop the carrots, parsnips, and potatoes into roughly 2-3 cm pieces. Mince the garlic and finely chop the fresh rosemary and thyme. In a large mixing bowl, toss the chopped vegetables with 15 ml of olive oil, half of the minced garlic, 3 g of salt, and 1 g of black pepper until evenly coated. Spread the seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Pat the pork tenderloin dry with paper towels. Rub the remaining 15 ml of olive oil over the pork, then coat it with the remaining minced garlic, rosemary, thyme, 2 g of salt, and 1 g of black pepper. Create a space on the baking sheet for the pork tenderloin amongst the vegetables. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the pork reaches 63°C. Add the fresh green beans to the baking sheet during the last 10 minutes of cooking. Once cooked, remove the pork from the oven, tent it loosely with foil, and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing and serving with the roasted vegetables.

title: Herb-Crusted Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["600 g Pork tenderloin, raw", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "300 g Carrots, raw", "200 g Parsnips, raw", "300 g Potatoes, white, raw", "4 clove Garlic, raw", "2 sprig Rosemary, fresh", "4 sprig Thyme, fresh", "5 g Salt, table", "2 g Black pepper, ground", "100 ml Chicken broth, low sodium"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Peel and chop the carrots, parsnips, and potatoes into bite-sized pieces. Mince three cloves of garlic and chop the fresh rosemary and thyme leaves. In a large bowl, toss the chopped vegetables with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, half of the minced garlic, half of the chopped herbs, 2.5 grams of salt, and 1 gram of black pepper. Spread the seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet and roast in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. While the vegetables roast, trim any silver skin from the pork tenderloin. Rub the tenderloin with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, the rest of the minced garlic, the remaining chopped herbs, 2.5 grams of salt, and 1 gram of black pepper. Heat an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork tenderloin for 2-3 minutes on each side until browned all over. Carefully remove the baking sheet with the vegetables from the oven, add the seared pork tenderloin to the sheet alongside the vegetables, and pour the chicken broth around the vegetables. Return the baking sheet to the oven and continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (medium-rare) or 71°C (medium). Once cooked, remove the pork from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent it loosely with foil. Let it rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing. Serve the sliced pork tenderloin alongside the roasted root vegetables and any pan juices.

title: Herb-Crusted Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Root Vegetables and Broccoli
ingredients_json: ["500 g Pork tenderloin, raw", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 tsp Dried rosemary", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "2 cloves Garlic, raw, fresh, crushed", "300 g Carrots, raw", "200 g Parsnips, raw", "300 g Sweet potato, raw", "300 g Broccoli, raw", "0.5 tsp Salt, table", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (390°F). In a small bowl, combine the Dijon mustard, 1 tablespoon of olive oil, dried rosemary, dried thyme, and crushed garlic to form a paste. Pat the pork tenderloin dry with paper towels, then rub the herb paste evenly over the entire surface. Peel and chop the carrots, parsnips, and sweet potato into bite-sized pieces. In a large roasting pan, toss the chopped root vegetables with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Place the herb-crusted pork tenderloin in the center of the roasting pan, nestled among the vegetables. Roast for 20 minutes. While the pork and root vegetables are roasting, cut the broccoli into florets. After 20 minutes, remove the roasting pan from the oven, stir the vegetables, and add the broccoli florets to the pan. Return to the oven and continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, or until the pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) and the vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized. Remove the pork from the pan, tent it loosely with foil, and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing. Serve the sliced pork alongside the roasted vegetables.

title: Mediterranean Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Root Vegetables and Lemon-Herb Sauce
ingredients_json: ["500 g Pork tenderloin, raw", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "200 g Carrot, raw", "200 g Potato, raw", "150 g Red onion, raw", "100 g Bell pepper, red, raw", "50 g Fresh parsley, chopped", "10 g Fresh thyme, chopped", "5 g Fresh rosemary, chopped", "2 cloves Garlic, raw", "0.5 piece Lemon, raw", "1 dl Chicken stock", "2 g Salt", "1 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. Pat the pork tenderloin dry with paper towels and season it evenly with salt and black pepper. In a large roasting pan, toss the carrots, potatoes, red onion, and bell pepper with half of the olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper. Arrange the vegetables in a single layer. Heat the remaining olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the pork tenderloin on all sides until nicely browned, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer the seared pork tenderloin to the roasting pan with the vegetables. Roast everything in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the pork reaches 63°C for medium-rare or 70°C for medium. While the pork and vegetables are roasting, prepare the sauce. Mince the garlic and finely chop the fresh parsley, thyme, and rosemary. Once the pork is done, remove it from the oven and transfer it to a cutting board to rest, loosely tented with foil, for at least 10 minutes. Leave the vegetables in the oven if they need a few more minutes to become tender. For the sauce, deglaze the skillet (if oven-safe) or a small saucepan over medium heat with the chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in the juice from half the lemon, the lemon zest, and all the fresh herbs. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until the sauce is slightly reduced. Slice the rested pork tenderloin into medallions. Serve the sliced pork with the roasted vegetables and drizzle generously with the vibrant lemon-herb sauce.

title: Hearty Chicken and Root Vegetable Pot Pie with Whole Wheat Crust
ingredients_json: ["500 g Chicken breast, skinless, raw", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "150 g Onion, raw", "200 g Carrot, raw", "150 g Celery, raw", "200 g Potato, white, raw", "100 g Green peas, frozen", "100 g Green beans, frozen", "50 g Whole wheat flour", "500 ml Chicken stock, low sodium", "200 ml Milk, semi-skimmed", "10 g Fresh thyme, leaves", "5 g Fresh parsley, leaves", "2 g Salt", "1 g Black pepper, ground", "250 g Whole wheat flour", "120 g Butter, unsalted", "5 g Salt", "80 ml Cold water"]
instructions: Begin by preparing the pie crust: In a large bowl or food processor, combine 250 g whole wheat flour with 5 g salt. Cut the cold butter into small cubes and add to the flour mixture. Mix until it resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add the cold water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until a dough forms. Do not overmix. Gather the dough into a disc, wrap it in cling film, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Next, prepare the filling: Cut the chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Dice the onion, carrots, celery, and potatoes into similar small pieces. Heat the olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned on all sides, then remove and set aside. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery to the pot and sauté for 5-7 minutes until they begin to soften. Stir in the diced potatoes and cook for another 5 minutes. Sprinkle 50 g of whole wheat flour over the vegetables and stir well, cooking for 1 minute to create a roux. Gradually whisk in the chicken stock and semi-skimmed milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps, until the mixture thickens and comes to a simmer. Return the cooked chicken to the pot. Stir in the frozen green peas, green beans, fresh thyme leaves, fresh parsley, 2 g salt, and black pepper. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is creamy. Preheat your oven to 200°C (390°F). Roll out the chilled pie dough on a lightly floured surface to fit a 23 cm pie dish. Pour the chicken and vegetable filling into the pie dish. Carefully place the rolled dough over the filling, trimming any excess and crimping the edges to seal. Cut a few small slits in the top of the crust to allow steam to escape during baking. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbling. Let the pot pie rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Lean Chicken and Root Vegetable Whole Wheat Pot Pie
ingredients_json: ["500 g Chicken fillet, without skin", "15 ml Olive oil", "150 g Onion, yellow, raw", "150 g Carrot, raw", "100 g Celery stalk, raw", "100 g Green peas, frozen", "100 g Sweet corn, frozen", "500 ml Chicken broth, low sodium", "60 g Whole wheat flour", "200 ml Milk, low fat, 1.5% fat", "5 g Fresh thyme, chopped", "5 g Fresh parsley, chopped", "2 g Salt", "1 g Black pepper", "1 sheet Whole wheat pie dough, ready-made, 140 g", "1 piece Egg, raw"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F). Cut the chicken fillets into 2 cm bite-sized pieces. Dice the onion, carrots, and celery into small, uniform pieces. Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the diced chicken and cook for 5-7 minutes until it is lightly browned on all sides; then remove the chicken from the pot and set it aside. Add the diced onion, carrots, and celery to the same pot and sauté for about 8-10 minutes until they are softened. Sprinkle the whole wheat flour over the vegetables and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to create a roux. Gradually whisk in the chicken broth and then the low-fat milk, ensuring no lumps form in the sauce. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens. Return the cooked chicken to the pot. Stir in the frozen green peas, frozen sweet corn, fresh thyme, fresh parsley, salt, and black pepper. Cook for another 5 minutes until all the vegetables are heated through and the sauce is well combined. Pour the chicken and vegetable filling into a 20 cm round pie dish. Carefully lay the single sheet of whole wheat pie dough over the filling, trimming any excess and crimping the edges to seal it securely around the rim of the dish. Make a few small slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape during baking. For a golden-brown finish, whisk the raw egg and brush it evenly over the top crust. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the crust is beautifully golden brown and the filling is bubbling hot. Allow the pot pie to rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Lean Chicken and Root Vegetable Whole Wheat Pot Pie
ingredients_json: ["250 g Whole wheat flour", "60 g Butter, unsalted", "100 ml Ice water", "2 g Salt, table", "300 g Chicken breast, raw, boneless, skinless", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "150 g Onion, yellow, raw", "100 g Carrot, raw", "100 g Celery, raw", "150 g Potato, raw, russet", "100 g Peas, green, frozen", "2 dl Chicken broth, low sodium", "50 g Whole wheat flour", "1.5 dl Milk, low-fat (1.5% fat)", "1 tbsp Fresh parsley, chopped", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "2 g Salt, table", "1 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: First, prepare the whole wheat pie crust. In a large bowl, combine 250 grams of whole wheat flour and 2 grams of salt. Cut the cold butter into small cubes and use your fingertips or a pastry blender to cut the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter remaining. Gradually add the 100 ml of ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form the dough into a disc, wrap it in plastic film, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Next, prepare the filling. Dice the 300 grams of chicken breast into 1.5 cm pieces. Chop the 150 grams of onion, 100 grams of carrot, and 100 grams of celery into small pieces. Peel and dice the 150 grams of potato into 1 cm cubes. Heat the 1 tbsp of olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the diced chicken and cook until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pot and set aside. Add the chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the same pot and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Stir in the diced potato and cook for another 3-5 minutes. Sprinkle the 50 grams of whole wheat flour over the vegetables and stir continuously for 1 minute to cook out the raw flour taste. Gradually whisk in the 2 dl of low-sodium chicken broth and then the 1.5 dl of low-fat milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring the mixture to a simmer, stirring occasionally, until it thickens, about 5 minutes. Return the cooked chicken to the pot. Stir in the 100 grams of frozen peas, 1 tbsp of fresh parsley, 1 tsp of dried thyme, 2 grams of salt, and 1 gram of black pepper. Cook for another 5 minutes, ensuring the vegetables are tender. Remove the filling from the heat and let it cool slightly. Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F). On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled pie dough into a circle large enough to cover the top of your pie dish (approximately 23 cm or 9-inch). Pour the cooled filling into a 23 cm pie dish. Carefully place the rolled-out dough over the filling. Trim any excess dough from the edges and crimp the edges to seal. Cut a few slits in the top of the crust to allow steam to escape during baking. Bake in the preheated oven for 30-35 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbling. If the crust starts to brown too quickly, you can cover the edges loosely with aluminum foil. Let the pot pie rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Healthy Chicken and Mixed Vegetable Whole Wheat Pot Pie
ingredients_json: ["500 g Chicken breast, boneless, skinless", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "150 g Onion, raw, chopped", "200 g Carrots, raw, diced", "150 g Celery, raw, diced", "200 g Green peas, frozen", "200 g Corn kernels, frozen", "200 g Green beans, fresh, trimmed and cut", "50 g Whole wheat flour", "600 ml Chicken broth, low sodium", "100 ml Milk, skimmed", "1 tsp Dried thyme", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "4 g Salt", "1 piece Egg, raw (for egg wash)", "180 g Whole wheat flour (for crust)", "80 g Butter, unsalted, cold, cubed (for crust)", "60 ml Ice water (for crust)", "2 g Salt (for crust)"]
instructions: Begin by preparing the whole wheat crust. In a large mixing bowl, combine 180g of whole wheat flour with 2g of salt. Add 80g of cold, cubed unsalted butter and cut it into the flour mixture using a pastry blender or your fingertips until it resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add 60ml of ice water, mixing gently until a shaggy dough forms. Be careful not to overmix. Gather the dough into a disc, wrap it in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for a minimum of 30 minutes. Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Dice 500g of chicken breast into 2 cm pieces. Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the chicken pieces and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned on all sides, which should take about 5-7 minutes. Remove the browned chicken from the skillet and set it aside. To the same skillet, add 150g of chopped onion, 200g of diced carrots, and 150g of diced celery. Sauté these vegetables for 5-7 minutes until they begin to soften. Stir in 50g of whole wheat flour and cook for another minute, stirring continuously, to create a roux. Gradually whisk in 600ml of low sodium chicken broth and 100ml of skimmed milk, making sure to eliminate any lumps. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently, until it thickens. Return the browned chicken to the skillet. Incorporate 200g of frozen green peas, 200g of frozen corn kernels, and 200g of trimmed and cut fresh green beans. Season the filling with 1 tsp of dried thyme, 0.5 tsp of ground black pepper, and 4g of salt. Stir everything thoroughly and remove the skillet from the heat. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled whole wheat dough into a circle that is slightly larger than the top of your skillet or pie dish. Carefully pour the chicken and vegetable filling into a 23 cm pie dish or keep it in the oven-safe skillet if you are using one. Gently place the rolled-out crust over the filling. Trim any excess dough and crimp the edges to seal the pie. Cut a few small slits in the top of the crust to allow steam to escape during baking. In a small bowl, whisk 1 raw egg and lightly brush it over the top of the pastry for a beautiful golden finish. Bake the pot pie for 30-35 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbly. Let the pot pie cool for about 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

title: Healthy Herb-Crusted Beef Pot Roast with Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Beef chuck roast, trimmed", "30 ml Olive oil", "300 g Onion, yellow, raw", "400 g Carrot, raw", "200 g Celery stalk, raw", "20 g Garlic clove, raw", "30 g Tomato paste", "700 ml Beef broth, low sodium", "200 ml Red wine, dry", "600 g Potato, red, raw", "10 g Fresh rosemary, chopped", "5 g Fresh thyme, chopped", "2 piece Bay leaf", "8 g Salt, table", "3 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Pat the beef chuck roast dry with paper towels and season generously with 6g of salt and 2g of black pepper. In a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot, heat 15ml of olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the beef on all sides until deeply browned, about 3-4 minutes per side, then remove the beef and set aside. Add the remaining 15ml of olive oil to the pot, then add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally. Add the minced garlic and tomato paste, cooking for another 2 minutes until fragrant. Deglaze the pot with the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom, and let it reduce by half, about 3-5 minutes. Stir in the beef broth, fresh rosemary, fresh thyme, and bay leaves. Return the seared beef to the pot, ensuring it is partially submerged in the liquid. Bring the liquid to a simmer, then cover the pot tightly and transfer it to the preheated oven. Cook for 2.5 hours. After 2.5 hours, add the whole small red potatoes around the beef in the pot. Cover again and continue to cook for another 1 to 1.5 hours, or until the beef is fork-tender and the potatoes are cooked through. Carefully remove the pot from the oven. Remove the beef and let it rest on a cutting board for 15-20 minutes before shredding or slicing. Skim any excess fat from the surface of the gravy, remove the bay leaves, and adjust seasoning with the remaining 2g of salt and 1g of black pepper if needed. Serve the shredded or sliced beef with the vegetables and gravy.

title: Lean Beef Pot Roast with Root Vegetables and Herbs
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Beef chuck roast, lean, trimmed", "15 ml Olive oil", "200 g Onion, yellow, raw", "300 g Carrots, raw", "200 g Celery stalk, raw", "500 g Potato, white, raw", "500 ml Beef broth, low sodium", "200 ml Red wine, dry", "2 cloves Garlic, raw", "5 g Thyme, fresh", "3 g Rosemary, fresh", "10 g Tomato paste", "5 g Salt", "2 g Black pepper, ground"]

title: Hearty Herb-Crusted Beef Pot Roast with Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1.2 kg Beef chuck roast, trimmed", "30 ml Olive oil", "8 g Salt, fine", "5 g Black pepper, ground", "400 g Onion, yellow, peeled", "20 g Garlic, cloves, peeled", "200 g Carrot, peeled", "200 g Celery, stalk", "30 g Tomato paste", "500 ml Beef broth, low sodium", "5 g Rosemary, fresh", "5 g Thyme, fresh", "600 g Potato, red, peeled", "300 g Parsnip, peeled"]
instructions: Begin by patting the beef chuck roast completely dry with paper towels. Generously season all sides of the beef with salt and black pepper. title: Hearty Braised Beef Pot Roast with Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Beef chuck roast, trimmed", "30 ml Olive oil", "200 g Onion, yellow, raw", "100 g Celery stalk, raw", "400 g Carrots, raw", "500 g Potatoes, white, raw", "200 g Mushrooms, cremini, raw", "4 cloves Garlic, raw", "15 g Tomato paste", "750 ml Beef broth, low sodium", "2 sprigs Thyme, fresh", "1 piece Bay leaf, dried", "10 g Salt, table", "2 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Begin by patting the trimmed beef chuck roast dry with paper towels, then generously season it all over with 8 grams of the salt and 1.5 grams of the black pepper. title: Hearty Herb-Crusted Beef Pot Roast with Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Beef chuck roast, lean", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "200 g Carrots, raw", "200 g Potatoes, raw, white", "150 g Celery, raw", "150 g Onion, yellow, raw", "4 cloves Garlic, raw", "500 ml Beef broth, low sodium", "50 g Tomato paste", "2 sprigs Fresh rosemary", "4 sprigs Fresh thyme", "5 g Salt, table", "2 g Black pepper, ground", "200 ml Water"]

title: Hearty Leek and Potato Soup with Fresh Herbs
ingredients_json: ["800 g Potato, white, raw, peeled", "300 g Leek, raw", "150 g Onion, raw", "20 g Garlic, raw", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "1500 ml Vegetable broth, low sodium", "200 ml Milk, semi-skimmed, 1.5% fat", "15 g Parsley, fresh", "3 g Salt", "2 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Begin by peeling and dicing the potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Thoroughly clean the leeks, trim off the dark green parts and the root, then slice them into thin rounds. Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic. Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and leeks, sautéing for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent, stirring occasionally. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the diced potatoes and pour in the low-sodium vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork. Once the potatoes are cooked, remove the pot from the heat. Carefully blend about half to two-thirds of the soup using an immersion blender directly in the pot, or transfer portions to a stand blender and blend until creamy, then return to the pot. Be cautious when blending hot liquids. Stir in the semi-skimmed milk, salt, and black pepper. Return the pot to low heat and gently warm through for 2-3 minutes, ensuring it does not boil after adding the milk. Chop the fresh parsley. Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish generously with the fresh parsley before serving warm.

title: Hearty Vegan Potato Leek and Spinach Soup
ingredients_json: ["15 ml Olive oil", "150 g Onion, yellow, raw", "300 g Leek, raw", "15 g Garlic, raw", "700 g Potato, white, raw", "1000 ml Vegetable broth, low sodium", "80 g Cashew nuts, raw", "150 g Spinach, raw", "5 g Thyme, fresh", "5 g Salt, table", "1 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Begin by heating the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sliced leeks (white and light green parts only, thoroughly washed) and sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Next, add the peeled and diced potatoes and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork. While the soup simmers, soak the cashews in hot water for at least 10 minutes (or overnight in cold water) to soften them. Drain the cashews and add them to a blender with a ladleful of the hot soup liquid. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Once the potatoes are tender, stir the cashew cream into the soup. Add the fresh spinach and thyme, stirring until the spinach wilts, which should only take a couple of minutes. Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. You can also use an immersion blender to lightly blend a portion of the soup for a creamier texture, leaving some potato chunks for body, or blend the entire soup until smooth if preferred. Serve hot.

title: Hearty Vegan Lentil and Potato Soup with Spinach
ingredients_json: ["2 tbsp Olive oil, extra virgin", "100 g Onion, yellow, raw, chopped", "150 g Carrots, raw, diced", "100 g Celery stalk, raw, diced", "2 cloves Garlic, raw, minced", "1 tsp Thyme, dried", "1 piece Bay leaf, dried", "500 g Potatoes, white, raw, peeled, diced", "150 g Lentils, red, dried", "1500 ml Vegetable broth, low sodium", "150 g Spinach, fresh, raw", "1.5 tsp Salt, table", "0.5 tsp Pepper, black, ground"]
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Stir in the minced garlic, dried thyme, and bay leaf, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Add the diced potatoes, red lentils, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the potatoes and lentils are tender. Remove and discard the bay leaf. Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup, leaving some chunks for texture, or mash with a potato masher for a chunkier soup. Stir in the fresh spinach until wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper to taste before serving hot.

title: Herb-Crusted Prime Rib with Garlic-Rosemary Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["2 kg Beef rib roast, bone-in", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "4 cloves Garlic, fresh, minced", "2 tbsp Fresh rosemary, chopped", "1 tbsp Fresh thyme, chopped", "20 g Coarse sea salt", "5 g Black pepper, ground", "500 g Potato, raw, peeled and cut into chunks", "300 g Carrot, raw, peeled and cut into chunks", "200 g Parsnip, raw, peeled and cut into chunks", "1 piece Red onion, cut into wedges", "2 tbsp Olive oil, for vegetables", "1 tbsp Fresh rosemary, for vegetables, chopped", "5 g Salt, for vegetables", "3 g Black pepper, ground, for vegetables"]
instructions: Allow the prime rib to sit at room temperature for at least 2 hours before cooking. Pat the roast completely dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine 2 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, 2 tbsp chopped fresh rosemary, 1 tbsp chopped fresh thyme, 20g coarse sea salt, and 5g ground black pepper to create a rub. Apply the rub generously all over the prime rib. Preheat your oven to 230°C. Place the prime rib, fat side up, in a roasting pan. Roast for 20 minutes at 230°C. Reduce the oven temperature to 135°C and continue roasting until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the roast (without touching bone) reads 52°C for rare, 57°C for medium-rare, or 60°C for medium. This will typically take 1.5 to 2.5 hours, depending on the roast size and desired doneness. While the prime rib is roasting, prepare the vegetables. In a large bowl, toss the potato, carrot, parsnip, and red onion chunks with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp chopped fresh rosemary, 5g salt, and 3g ground black pepper. When the prime rib is almost done, or about 45 minutes before serving, add the seasoned root vegetables to a separate baking sheet or around the prime rib in the roasting pan if there's space. Roast the vegetables for 30-45 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned, turning halfway through. Once the prime rib reaches the desired internal temperature, remove it from the oven, tent loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving. Resting is crucial for juicy meat. Slice the prime rib against the grain and serve with the roasted root vegetables.

title: Herb-Crusted Prime Rib with Roasted Root Vegetables and Pan Sauce
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Beef, prime rib roast, lean, bone-in", "30 ml Olive oil", "20 g Garlic, cloves, minced", "10 g Rosemary, fresh, chopped", "5 g Thyme, fresh, chopped", "10 g Salt, fine", "5 g Black pepper, ground", "500 g Potato, red, unpeeled, cut into chunks", "300 g Carrot, raw, peeled, cut into chunks", "200 g Parsnip, raw, peeled, cut into chunks", "150 g Onion, yellow, roughly chopped", "250 ml Beef broth, low sodium"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). In a small bowl, combine the olive oil, minced garlic, chopped fresh rosemary, thyme, salt, and black pepper to create an aromatic herb paste. Pat the prime rib roast thoroughly dry with paper towels, which helps create a beautiful crust, then generously rub the herb paste all over the entire surface of the roast. Place the prime rib, fat-side up, in a large roasting pan. In a separate bowl, toss the potato, carrot, parsnip, and onion chunks with a small amount of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper, then arrange them around the prime rib in the roasting pan. Roast for 20 minutes at the high temperature of 220°C (425°F) to sear the exterior of the meat. After searing, reduce the oven temperature to 160°C (325°F) and continue roasting until a meat thermometer, inserted into the thickest part of the roast while avoiding the bone, reads 52°C (125°F) for rare, 57°C (135°F) for medium-rare, or 63°C (145°F) for medium. This process typically takes approximately 1.5 to 2.5 hours, depending on your desired doneness and the specific calibration of your oven. Once the desired internal temperature is reached, carefully remove the roast from the oven, transfer it to a clean cutting board, tent it loosely with aluminum foil, and allow it to rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving; the internal temperature will continue to rise during this resting period. While the roast rests, pour the low-sodium beef broth into the roasting pan, scraping up any delicious browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon to create a simple yet flavorful pan sauce. Serve the beautifully carved prime rib with the tender roasted root vegetables and a drizzle of the homemade pan sauce.

title: Lean Herb-Crusted Prime Rib with Roasted Root Vegetables and Light Au Jus
ingredients_json: ["1.2 kg Beef, prime rib roast, boneless, trimmed lean", "3 tbsp Olive oil, extra virgin", "20 g Garlic, raw, minced", "15 g Fresh rosemary, chopped", "10 g Fresh thyme, chopped", "10 g Salt, fine", "5 g Black pepper, ground", "400 g Carrots, raw, peeled, cut into chunks", "400 g Parsnips, raw, peeled, cut into chunks", "600 g Potatoes, white, raw, peeled, cut into chunks", "300 g Asparagus, raw, trimmed", "300 ml Beef broth, low sodium", "1 dl Red wine, dry"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 230°C. In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons of olive oil with the minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, salt, and black pepper to form a paste. Pat the prime rib dry with paper towels and rub the herb paste all over the surface of the roast. Place the prime rib fat-side up in a roasting pan. In a large bowl, toss the carrots, parsnips, and potatoes with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper, then spread them in a single layer around the prime rib in the roasting pan. Roast for 15 minutes at 230°C. Reduce the oven temperature to 150°C and continue roasting for approximately 1.5 to 2 hours, or until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the roast (avoiding bone if applicable) reads 52-54°C for medium-rare. During the last 15 minutes of roasting, add the asparagus to the pan with the root vegetables. Once cooked, remove the prime rib from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes; this is crucial for juicy meat. While the meat rests, prepare the au jus: Carefully pour off most of the fat from the roasting pan, leaving the pan drippings and any browned bits. Place the pan over medium heat on the stovetop. Pour in the red wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon, deglazing for 2 minutes. Add the beef broth and bring to a simmer, cooking until reduced slightly, about 5-7 minutes. Strain the au jus into a serving bowl. Slice the rested prime rib against the grain and serve immediately with the roasted vegetables and au jus.

title: Herb-Crusted Prime Rib with Roasted Root Vegetables
ingredients_json: ["1.5 kg Beef, prime rib roast, boneless, lean", "30 ml Olive oil", "20 g Rosemary, fresh", "15 g Thyme, fresh", "4 cloves Garlic, raw", "10 g Salt, table", "5 g Black pepper, ground", "500 g Potato, white, raw, with skin", "300 g Carrot, raw", "200 g Parsnip, raw", "1 piece Onion, yellow, large", "100 ml Beef broth, low sodium"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 230°C. Pat the prime rib roast thoroughly dry with paper towels. Rub this mixture evenly over the entire surface of the prime rib. Place the roast, fat side up, in a large roasting pan. Roast in the preheated oven for 20 minutes to create a crust. While the prime rib is searing, prepare the vegetables. Peel and chop the potatoes, carrots, parsnips, and onion into roughly 2-3 cm pieces. Toss the chopped vegetables with the remaining 15 ml of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper in a large bowl. After the initial 20 minutes, reduce the oven temperature to 160°C. Add the seasoned root vegetables to the roasting pan around the prime rib. Continue roasting, basting the meat occasionally with pan juices, until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the roast (without touching bone) reads 52-54°C for medium-rare, or to your desired doneness. This will typically take an additional 1.5 to 2 hours, depending on your roast's starting temperature and oven. During the last 30 minutes of roasting, pour the low-sodium beef broth over the vegetables and into the pan to add moisture and flavor. Once cooked to your liking, remove the prime rib from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving; this allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a tender and moist roast. While the meat rests, you can increase the oven temperature slightly to crisp up the vegetables further if desired. Carve the prime rib against the grain into thick slices and serve immediately with the roasted root vegetables and pan juices.

title: Healthy Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork with Apple Cider Vinegar Slaw and Whole Wheat Buns
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Pork loin, boneless", "1 tbsp Smoked paprika powder", "1 tbsp Garlic powder", "1 tbsp Onion powder", "1 tsp Cumin powder", "0.5 tsp Cayenne pepper powder", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "2.5 g Salt, table", "240 ml Chicken broth, low sodium", "60 ml Apple cider vinegar", "2 tbsp Tomato paste", "1 tbsp Maple syrup", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "1 piece Bay leaf", "300 g Cabbage, white, shredded", "150 g Carrot, shredded", "60 ml Apple cider vinegar", "2 tbsp Olive oil", "1 tbsp Maple syrup", "1.25 g Salt, table", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground", "4 pieces Whole wheat buns", "100 g Pickle, cucumber, sliced"]
instructions: Begin by patting the pork loin dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, cayenne pepper, black pepper, and 2.5 grams of salt. Rub this spice mixture generously over all sides of the pork loin. Place the seasoned pork into your slow cooker. In a separate bowl, whisk together the low sodium chicken broth, 60 ml of apple cider vinegar, tomato paste, 1 tbsp maple syrup, and Dijon mustard. Pour this liquid over the pork in the slow cooker, then add the bay leaf. Cover and cook on the low setting for 6-8 hours, or on the high setting for 3-4 hours, until the pork is exceptionally tender and can be easily shredded with a fork. Once cooked, carefully remove the pork from the slow cooker and place it on a clean cutting board. Using two forks, shred the pork into desired strands. Skim any excess fat from the cooking liquid in the slow cooker, then return the shredded pork to the pot and toss it with the sauce to ensure it's well coated and flavorful. While the pork is cooking, or during its final hour, prepare the apple cider vinegar slaw. In a large mixing bowl, combine the shredded white cabbage and grated carrots. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 60 ml of apple cider vinegar, olive oil, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1.25 grams of salt, and 0.25 tsp of black pepper to create the dressing. Pour this dressing over the cabbage and carrot mixture and toss thoroughly to combine. Allow the slaw to sit for at least 15 minutes to marinate and meld the flavors. To serve, lightly toast the whole wheat buns. Pile a generous portion of the saucy pulled pork onto the bottom half of each bun, top with a spoonful of the crisp apple cider vinegar slaw, and cover with the top bun. Serve immediately, accompanied by sliced cucumber pickles if desired.

title: Lean Slow Cooker Pulled Pork with Whole Wheat Buns and Greek Yogurt Slaw
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Pork shoulder, boneless, lean", "200 g Onion, yellow", "15 g Garlic, raw", "400 g Tomatoes, crushed, canned", "60 ml Apple cider vinegar", "30 ml Maple syrup", "15 g Smoked paprika, ground", "5 g Mustard powder", "5 g Cumin, ground", "2 g Black pepper, ground", "4 g Salt, table", "120 ml Water", "6 pieces Burger bun, whole wheat", "300 g Cabbage, white, raw", "150 g Carrot, raw", "120 ml Greek yogurt, plain, low fat", "30 ml Mayonnaise, light", "15 ml Apple cider vinegar", "1.5 g Salt, table", "1 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions:
Start by patting the pork shoulder dry. In a small bowl, combine the smoked paprika, mustard powder, ground cumin, 4g salt, and 2g black pepper to create a rub. Generously coat the pork shoulder with this spice rub. Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Place the diced onion and minced garlic in the bottom of a slow cooker. Add the seasoned pork shoulder on top. Pour in the crushed tomatoes, 60ml apple cider vinegar, 30ml maple syrup, and 120ml water around the pork. Cover the slow cooker and cook on low for 6-8 hours, or on high for 3-4 hours, until the pork is very tender and easily shreds with a fork.

While the pork is cooking, prepare the coleslaw. Finely shred the white cabbage and grate the carrots. In a medium bowl, whisk together the low-fat Greek yogurt, light mayonnaise, 15ml apple cider vinegar, 1.5g salt, and 1g black pepper until smooth. Add the shredded cabbage and grated carrots to the dressing and toss well to combine. Cover and refrigerate until serving.

Once the pork is cooked, carefully remove it from the slow cooker and place it on a large cutting board or in a shallow dish. Using two forks, shred the pork into small pieces, discarding any large pieces of fat. Skim any excess fat from the cooking liquid in the slow cooker, then return the shredded pork to the slow cooker and stir it into the sauce to coat thoroughly. Cook on warm for an additional 15-30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

To serve, lightly toast the whole wheat burger buns. Divide the pulled pork among the toasted buns, and top each with a generous spoonful of the Greek yogurt slaw. Serve immediately.

title: Healthy Slow-Cooker Chipotle Pulled Pork with Crunchy Coleslaw
ingredients_json: ["1.2 kg Pork shoulder, boneless, lean", "150 g Tomato paste", "100 ml Apple cider vinegar", "30 ml Maple syrup, pure", "2 tbsp Chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, minced", "1 tbsp Smoked paprika", "1 tbsp Cumin powder", "1 tsp Garlic powder", "1 tsp Onion powder", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "0.5 tsp Salt", "250 ml Chicken broth, low sodium", "500 g Cabbage, green, shredded", "200 g Carrot, raw, shredded", "100 ml Greek yoghurt, plain, low fat", "30 ml Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "0.25 tsp Salt", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground", "6 pieces Whole wheat buns"]

Place the lean pork shoulder in a slow cooker and pour the prepared sauce over it, ensuring the pork is thoroughly coated. Add the low-sodium chicken broth to the slow cooker. Cover and cook on a low setting for 6 to 8 hours, or on a high setting for 3 to 4 hours, until the pork is exceedingly tender and can be easily shredded with two forks. Once cooked, carefully remove the pork from the slow cooker and place it on a cutting board. Using two forks, shred the pork completely, then return the shredded meat to the slow cooker and stir it into the flavorful cooking liquid to absorb all the juices. While the pork is cooking, prepare the coleslaw by combining the shredded green cabbage and shredded carrot in a large mixing bowl. In a separate small bowl, whisk together the low-fat Greek yogurt, 30 ml apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, 0.25 tsp salt, and 0.25 tsp black pepper until the dressing is smooth and well combined. Pour the dressing over the cabbage and carrot mixture and toss vigorously to ensure all vegetables are evenly coated. To serve, spoon a generous portion of the warm pulled pork onto each whole wheat bun and top with a hearty scoop of the fresh, crunchy coleslaw.

title: Lean Pulled Pork with Tangy Cabbage Slaw on Whole Wheat Buns
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Pork shoulder, lean, boneless", "150 g Onion, yellow", "30 g Garlic, raw", "10 g Paprika powder, sweet", "5 g Cumin powder", "2 g Chili powder, mild", "2 g Black pepper, ground", "5 g Salt, table", "240 ml Chicken broth, low sodium", "60 ml Apple cider vinegar", "30 ml Tomato paste", "15 ml Olive oil", "6 pieces Whole wheat hamburger buns", "300 g Cabbage, green, raw", "150 g Carrot, raw", "60 ml Greek yogurt, plain, low fat", "30 ml Mayonnaise, light", "15 ml Lemon juice, fresh", "2 g Dill, fresh"]
instructions: Pat the pork shoulder dry and season it evenly with 3g of salt, paprika, cumin, chili powder, and black pepper. In a large oven-safe pot or slow cooker insert, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the pork on all sides until browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the pork and set aside. Add the chopped onion to the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and tomato paste, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Deglaze the pot with apple cider vinegar, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Stir in the low-sodium chicken broth and the remaining 2g of salt. Return the seared pork to the pot. If using a slow cooker, cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 3-4 hours, until the pork is fork-tender and easily shreds. If using an oven, cover the pot tightly and cook at 150°C (300°F) for 3-4 hours. Once cooked, remove the pork from the liquid and shred it using two forks. Return the shredded pork to the sauce in the pot, stirring to combine. While the pork is cooking, prepare the slaw. Finely shred the green cabbage and grate the carrot. In a medium bowl, whisk together the low-fat Greek yogurt, light mayonnaise, fresh lemon juice, and chopped fresh dill. Season the dressing with a pinch of salt and pepper. Add the shredded cabbage and grated carrot to the dressing and toss until well combined. Serve the warm pulled pork piled high on whole wheat hamburger buns, topped with a generous portion of the tangy cabbage slaw.

title: Healthy Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork with Tangy Coleslaw and Wholewheat Buns
ingredients_json: ["1 kg Pork loin, boneless, trimmed", "1 tbsp Paprika powder", "1 tbsp Garlic powder", "1 tsp Onion powder", "1 tsp Cumin, ground", "0.5 tsp Black pepper, ground", "2 g Salt", "200 g Tomato passata", "2 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Honey", "1 tbsp Dijon mustard", "1 tsp Worcestershire sauce", "0.5 tsp Smoked paprika", "0.25 tsp Cayenne pepper", "200 g White cabbage, shredded", "100 g Carrot, shredded", "50 g Red onion, thinly sliced", "3 tbsp Apple cider vinegar", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "1 tsp Honey", "1 g Salt", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground", "4 pieces Wholewheat burger buns", "4 pieces Lettuce leaves, Romaine"]
instructions: Begin by preparing the pork. Trim any excess visible fat from the pork loin. In a small bowl, combine the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, ground cumin, black pepper, and 2 grams of salt to create a spice rub. Rub this mixture generously all over the pork loin. Place the seasoned pork in a slow cooker. In a separate bowl, whisk together the tomato passata, 2 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar, 1 tablespoon of honey, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper to make the BBQ sauce. Pour about half of this sauce over the pork in the slow cooker. Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours, or on high for 3-4 hours, until the pork is very tender and easily shreds with a fork. Once cooked, remove the pork from the slow cooker and place it on a cutting board. Using two forks, shred the pork into small pieces. Return the shredded pork to the slow cooker with the remaining cooking liquid and the rest of the prepared BBQ sauce, stirring to combine. Keep warm on the 'warm' setting while you prepare the coleslaw. For the coleslaw, combine the shredded white cabbage, shredded carrot, and thinly sliced red onion in a large bowl. In a small bowl, whisk together the 3 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar, olive oil, 1 teaspoon of honey, 1 gram of salt, and 0.25 teaspoon of black pepper for the dressing. Pour the dressing over the cabbage mixture and toss well to coat. To serve, lightly toast the wholewheat burger buns if desired. Place a Romaine lettuce leaf on the bottom half of each bun, then pile a generous portion of the saucy pulled pork on top. Finish with a spoonful of the tangy coleslaw and cap with the top half of the bun.

title: Spicy Chicken and Black Bean Quesadillas with Creamy Avocado Dip
ingredients_json: ["200 g Chicken breast, raw, boneless, skinless", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "120 g Onion, yellow, raw", "150 g Bell pepper, red, raw", "100 g Black beans, canned, drained, rinsed", "1 tsp Cumin, ground", "0.5 tsp Paprika, ground", "0.25 tsp Chilli powder", "0.25 tsp Salt, table", "0.15 tsp Black pepper, ground", "2 pieces Tortilla, whole wheat, 20 cm diameter", "80 g Cheese, mozzarella, low fat, shredded", "0.5 piece Avocado, raw", "60 g Greek yogurt, plain, low fat", "1 tbsp Lime juice, fresh"]
instructions: Begin by dicing the chicken breast into small, bite-sized pieces. Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook until it's browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. While the chicken cooks, finely dice the onion and bell pepper. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside. Add the diced onion and bell pepper to the same pan, cooking until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the drained and rinsed black beans, ground cumin, paprika, chilli powder, salt, and black pepper. Cook for another 2 minutes, allowing the spices to become fragrant. Return the cooked chicken to the pan and mix well with the vegetable and bean mixture. To assemble the quesadillas, lay one whole wheat tortilla flat on a clean surface or a separate large, dry pan over medium heat. Sprinkle half of the shredded low-fat mozzarella over one half of the tortilla, then spoon half of the chicken and black bean mixture evenly over the cheese. Fold the other half of the tortilla over the filling. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, or until the tortilla is golden brown and the cheese is melted and bubbly. Repeat with the remaining tortilla and filling. While the quesadillas cook, prepare the avocado dip: scoop the flesh from the avocado half into a small bowl, add the Greek yogurt, fresh lime juice, and a tiny pinch of salt. Mash with a fork or blend until smooth and creamy. Once cooked, slice each quesadilla into wedges and serve immediately with the creamy avocado dip.

title: Spicy Chicken and Black Bean Quesadillas with Avocado Crema
ingredients_json: ["150 g Chicken breast, raw, boneless, skinless", "2 pieces Tortilla, whole wheat, large", "100 g Black beans, canned, rinsed and drained", "75 g Bell pepper, red, fresh", "50 g Onion, yellow, fresh", "60 g Cheese, mozzarella, low-fat", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "0.5 tsp Cumin, ground", "0.5 tsp Chili powder", "2 tbsp Water", "60 g Avocado, fresh", "30 g Yogurt, Greek, plain, 0% fat", "1 tbsp Lime juice, fresh", "2 g Salt, table", "0.5 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Slice the chicken breast into thin strips and dice the bell pepper and onion. Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, cumin, chili powder, 1 gram of salt, and black pepper, cooking until the chicken is browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the diced bell pepper, onion, black beans, and water, then cook for another 5 minutes until the vegetables soften slightly and the liquid has evaporated. Remove the filling from the pan and set aside. Wipe the pan clean. To prepare the avocado crema, mash the avocado in a small bowl with the Greek yogurt, lime juice, and remaining 1 gram of salt until smooth. Heat the same pan over medium heat. Place one whole wheat tortilla in the pan, sprinkle half of the low-fat mozzarella over one half of the tortilla, then spoon half of the chicken and bean filling onto the cheesy side. Fold the empty half of the tortilla over the filling and gently press down. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, or until the tortilla is golden brown and the cheese is melted. Repeat with the second tortilla and remaining filling and cheese. Slice each quesadilla in half or into wedges and serve immediately with a dollop of fresh avocado crema.

title: Spicy Chicken, Black Bean, and Corn Quesadillas with Avocado-Lime Crema
ingredients_json: ["200 g Chicken breast, raw, boneless, skinless", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "80 g Onion, raw, chopped", "80 g Bell pepper, red, raw, chopped", "80 g Corn, frozen, kernels", "150 g Black beans, canned, drained, rinsed", "1 tsp Cumin, ground", "0.5 tsp Chili powder", "0.25 tsp Salt", "0.1 tsp Black pepper, ground", "4 pieces Tortillas, whole wheat, medium (approx. 40g each)", "80 g Cheese, low-fat, shredded", "1 piece Avocado, raw, small (approx. 100g)", "0.8 dl Greek yogurt, plain, low-fat", "1 tbsp Lime juice, fresh", "5 g Coriander, fresh, chopped"]
instructions: Start by dicing the chicken breast into small, bite-sized pieces. Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Add the diced chicken and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it is browned and cooked through. Once cooked, remove the chicken from the pan and set it aside. In the same pan, add the chopped onion and bell pepper, cooking for about 5 minutes until they have softened. Stir in the frozen corn kernels, the drained and rinsed black beans, ground cumin, chili powder, salt, and black pepper. Cook this mixture for another 3-5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together. Return the cooked chicken to the pan and mix it well with the vegetable and bean mixture. To assemble the quesadillas, wipe out the pan if necessary, then place one whole wheat tortilla in the pan over medium-low heat. Sprinkle half of the shredded low-fat cheese over one half of the tortilla. Spoon approximately one quarter of the chicken and vegetable mixture onto the cheesy half. Carefully fold the other half of the tortilla over the filling to create a half-moon shape. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until the tortilla is golden brown and crispy, and the cheese is thoroughly melted and bubbly. Remove the cooked quesadilla from the pan and repeat this process with the remaining tortillas, cheese, and filling to make a total of four half-moon quesadillas. While the quesadillas are cooking, prepare the avocado-lime crema. In a small bowl, mash the avocado with a fork until mostly smooth. Stir in the low-fat Greek yogurt, fresh lime juice, and finely chopped fresh coriander until all ingredients are well combined and creamy. Serve the warm quesadillas immediately, accompanied by a generous dollop of the fresh avocado-lime crema.

title: Hearty Chicken and Black Bean Quesadillas with Avocado Crema
ingredients_json: ["300 g Chicken fillet, without skin, raw", "4 pieces Tortilla, whole wheat", "150 g Bell pepper, red, raw", "80 g Onion, raw", "200 g Black beans, canned, drained", "100 g Corn, frozen", "80 g Cheese, hard, low fat, e.g. mozzarella light", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "1 tsp Cumin, ground", "1 tsp Paprika, smoked", "0.5 tsp Garlic powder", "0.5 tsp Chili powder", "3 g Salt, table", "1 g Pepper, black, ground", "150 g Avocado, raw", "0.5 piece Lime, raw", "15 g Coriander, fresh, raw"]
instructions: Begin by dicing the chicken fillet into small, bite-sized pieces and season them with half of the salt and pepper. Finely chop the red bell pepper and onion. While the filling is hot, prepare the avocado crema: mash the avocado in a small bowl, then stir in the juice from half a lime and the fresh chopped coriander until smooth. To assemble the quesadillas, lay one whole wheat tortilla in a clean, dry skillet over medium heat. Spoon about a quarter of the chicken and bean mixture onto one half of the tortilla, then sprinkle generously with about 20 grams of the low-fat cheese. Fold the other half of the tortilla over the filling and press down gently with a spatula. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, or until the tortilla is golden brown and the cheese is melted and bubbly. Repeat with the remaining tortillas and filling. Slice each quesadilla in half or into wedges and serve immediately with a dollop of the homemade avocado crema.

title: Healthy Chicken and Spinach Quesadillas with Avocado Crema
ingredients_json: ["4 pieces Tortilla, whole wheat, medium (approx 20cm diameter)", "200 g Chicken breast, raw, boneless, skinless", "100 g Spinach, fresh", "100 g Mushrooms, white, raw", "50 g Onion, yellow, raw", "50 g Bell pepper, red, raw", "80 g Cheese, mozzarella, low fat, shredded", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "1 g Cumin, ground", "1 g Paprika, smoked", "1 g Garlic powder", "0.5 g Chilli powder", "2 g Salt", "0.5 g Black pepper, ground", "1 piece Avocado, medium (approx 150g)", "50 ml Water", "1 tbsp Lime juice, fresh"]
instructions: Begin by preparing the chicken and vegetables. Dice the chicken breast into small, bite-sized pieces. Finely chop the onion and bell pepper, and slice the mushrooms. Heat half a tablespoon of olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the diced chicken along with the cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, chilli powder, half a gram of salt, and a quarter gram of black pepper. Cook until the chicken is browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside. In the same pan, add the remaining half tablespoon of olive oil. Add the chopped onion, bell pepper, and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened, then add the fresh spinach and cook until wilted. Return the cooked chicken to the pan with the vegetables, stir to combine, and set the filling aside. To prepare the avocado crema, scoop the flesh of the avocado into a small bowl or food processor. Add the lime juice, 50 ml of water, and the remaining 1.5 grams of salt and quarter gram of black pepper. Mash with a fork or blend until smooth and creamy. To assemble the quesadillas, wipe out the pan. Place one whole wheat tortilla in the dry pan over medium heat. Sprinkle a quarter of the shredded low-fat mozzarella over one half of the tortilla. Spoon a quarter of the chicken and vegetable filling over the cheese, then top with another quarter of the cheese. Fold the empty half of the tortilla over the filling. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, or until the tortilla is golden brown and the cheese is melted and bubbly. Repeat this process for the remaining three tortillas, creating two full quesadillas. Slice each quesadilla into wedges and serve immediately with a generous dollop of the fresh avocado crema.

title: Whole Wheat Ricotta and Spinach Ravioli with Fresh Tomato and Basil Sauce
ingredients_json: ["300 g Whole wheat ricotta and spinach ravioli", "400 g Canned chopped tomatoes, no added salt", "100 g Fresh spinach", "1 piece Onion, medium", "2 cloves Garlic", "30 ml Olive oil", "10 g Fresh basil leaves", "30 g Parmesan cheese, grated", "50 ml Vegetable broth, low sodium", "0.5 g Salt, table", "0.5 g Black pepper, ground"]
instructions: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. While the water heats, prepare the tomato sauce. In a large pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until it becomes softened and translucent, which should take about 5 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until it is fragrant, making sure not to burn it. Pour in the canned chopped tomatoes and the vegetable broth. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and let it cook for about 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Season the sauce with salt and black pepper. Meanwhile, add the ravioli to the boiling water and cook according to package instructions, typically 3-5 minutes, until they are al dente. While the ravioli cooks, stir the fresh spinach into the tomato sauce, allowing it to wilt for 1-2 minutes. Drain the cooked ravioli thoroughly and gently add it directly to the pan with the sauce. Toss gently to coat the ravioli evenly with the sauce. Stir in the fresh basil leaves just before serving. Serve immediately, garnished with grated Parmesan cheese.

title: Hearty & Healthy Homemade Refried Pinto Beans
ingredients_json: ["800 g Pinto beans, canned, rinsed and drained", "1 tbsp Olive oil, extra virgin", "100 g Onion, yellow, raw, chopped", "20 g Garlic, raw, minced", "1.5 dl Vegetable broth, low sodium", "5 g Cumin, ground", "5 g Chili powder", "2 g Salt, table", "0.5 dl Water", "1 piece Lime, juice of", "15 g Coriander, fresh, chopped"]
instructions: Begin by heating the olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for about 5-7 minutes until it becomes translucent and soft. Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it. Add the rinsed and drained pinto beans to the skillet along with the vegetable broth, ground cumin, chili powder, and salt. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Once simmering, reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the beans to soften further. Uncover the pot and use a potato masher or a fork to mash the beans to your desired consistency. For a smoother texture, you can blend about half of the beans in a food processor and then return them to the pot. If the mixture seems too thick, gradually add the 0.5 dl of water or more broth until it reaches a creamy consistency. Stir in the fresh lime juice. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped coriander.

title: Hearty Black Bean Refried Beans with Aromatics
ingredients_json: ["500 g Black beans, cooked", "1 tbsp Olive oil", "100 g Onion, yellow, raw, chopped", "2 cloves Garlic, raw, minced", "1 tsp Cumin powder", "0.5 tsp Chili powder", "1 dl Vegetable broth, low sodium", "0.5 tsp Salt", "0.25 tsp Black pepper, ground"]

Continue to cook for 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the refried beans are hot and slightly thickened. Serve warm as a side or main dish.

title: Hearty Smoky Black Bean Refried Beans with Fresh Lime and Coriander
ingredients_json: ["400 g Black beans, canned, drained, rinsed", "15 ml Olive oil, extra virgin", "100 g Onion, yellow, raw, finely chopped", "10 g Garlic, raw, minced", "2 g Cumin powder, ground", "1 g Chili powder, mild", "0.5 g Smoked paprika, sweet", "200 ml Vegetable broth, low sodium", "50 ml Water, tap", "2 g Salt, table", "0.5 g Black pepper, ground", "15 g Fresh coriander, chopped", "30 ml Lime juice, fresh"]

title: Zesty Black Bean Refried Beans with Fresh Herbs
ingredients_json: ["400 g Black beans, canned, drained and rinsed", "15 ml Olive oil, extra virgin", "100 g Onion, yellow, chopped", "15 g Garlic, raw, minced", "2 g Cumin powder", "1 g Chili powder", "0.5 g Oregano, dried", "120 ml Vegetable broth, low sodium", "30 ml Lime juice, fresh", "15 g Cilantro, fresh, chopped", "2 g Salt, table", "0.5 g Black pepper, ground"]

title: Hearty Black Bean Refried Beans with Smoky Chipotle
ingredients_json: ["400 g Black beans, canned, drained, rinsed", "10 ml Olive oil, extra virgin", "100 g Onion, yellow, raw, chopped", "15 g Garlic, raw, minced", "100 ml Vegetable broth, low sodium", "5 g Cumin powder", "3 g Chili powder", "1 g Smoked paprika", "1 g Salt, table", "0.5 g Black pepper, ground", "10 g Lime juice, fresh", "15 g Coriander leaves, fresh, chopped"]

Stir in the minced garlic, cumin powder, chili powder, and smoked paprika, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Add the drained and rinsed black beans to the saucepan along with the vegetable broth, salt, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the beans to soften further. Remove from heat.
