title: Healthy Dark Chocolate Avocado Mousse
ingredients_json: ["2 pieces Avocado, raw", "60 g Cocoa powder, unsweetened", "80 ml Maple syrup", "150 ml Almond drink, unsweetened", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "1 g Salt, table"]
instructions: Halve and pit the avocados, then scoop the flesh into a high-speed blender. Add the unsweetened cocoa powder, maple syrup, almond drink, vanilla extract, and salt to the blender. Blend on high speed until the mixture is completely smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides of the blender with a spatula as needed to ensure no lumps of avocado remain. Taste the mousse and adjust the sweetness if desired by adding a little more maple syrup. Pour the finished mousse into four individual serving dishes or ramekins. Cover each dish with plastic wrap or a lid and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until thoroughly chilled and set. Serve cold, optionally garnished with fresh berries or a light dusting of extra cocoa powder.

title: Creamy Dark Chocolate Avocado Mousse
ingredients_json: ["2 pieces Avocado, raw, unspecified", "50 g Cocoa powder, unsweetened", "60 ml Maple syrup", "120 ml Almond milk, unsweetened", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "1 g Salt, table"]
instructions: Halve the avocados and scoop the flesh into a food processor. Add the cocoa powder, maple syrup, unsweetened almond milk, vanilla extract, and salt. Process on high speed until the mixture is completely smooth and creamy, scraping down the sides as needed to ensure no lumps remain. This may take 2-3 minutes. Once smooth, spoon the mousse into individual serving dishes or ramekins. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2 hours, to allow it to firm up and chill thoroughly before serving.

title: Creamy Dark Chocolate Avocado Mousse with Raspberry Coulis
ingredients_json: ["300 g Avocado, raw, flesh", "50 g Cocoa powder, unsweetened", "60 ml Maple syrup, pure", "5 ml Vanilla extract, pure", "120 ml Almond drink, unsweetened", "1 g Salt, table", "200 g Raspberries, fresh or frozen", "15 ml Lemon juice, fresh", "15 ml Maple syrup, pure"]
instructions:
Begin by preparing the chocolate mousse. Halve the avocados, remove the pits, and scoop the flesh into a high-speed blender or food processor. Add the unsweetened cocoa powder, 60 ml of maple syrup, vanilla extract, unsweetened almond drink, and a pinch of salt to the blender. Blend on high until the mixture is completely smooth and creamy, scraping down the sides as needed to ensure no lumps remain. The texture should be akin to a rich, thick mousse. Divide the mousse evenly into four small serving bowls or glasses, then cover them and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until thoroughly chilled and set.

While the mousse is chilling, prepare the raspberry coulis. Combine the raspberries (fresh or frozen), 15 ml of lemon juice, and 15 ml of maple syrup in a small saucepan over medium heat. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally, and cook for about 5-7 minutes, until the raspberries have softened and broken down, forming a syrupy sauce. Remove the saucepan from the heat and, if desired, press the coulis through a fine-mesh sieve to remove the seeds, resulting in a smooth sauce. Allow the coulis to cool completely.

Once the chocolate avocado mousse is well-chilled, drizzle a generous amount of the cooled raspberry coulis over each serving. Garnish with a few fresh raspberries if desired, and serve immediately.

title: Healthy Mixed Berry Yogurt Mousse
ingredients_json: ["500 g Yogurt, Greek, plain, low-fat", "200 g Mixed berries, frozen, unsweetened", "30 ml Maple syrup, pure", "10 g Gelatin powder, unflavored", "60 ml Water, tap", "5 ml Lemon juice, fresh"]
instructions: First, bloom the gelatin by sprinkling the gelatin powder over the cold water in a small heatproof bowl and let it sit for 5 minutes until it thickens. Meanwhile, gently heat the mixed berries in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until they soften and release their juices, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat and mash the berries slightly with a fork or potato masher, then stir in the maple syrup and lemon juice. Once the gelatin has bloomed, place the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie) and stir until the gelatin is completely dissolved and clear. Be careful not to boil it. Pour the dissolved gelatin into the berry mixture and stir well to combine. Let this mixture cool down slightly, but not set. In a large mixing bowl, gently fold the low-fat Greek yogurt into the berry and gelatin mixture until everything is well combined and the color is uniform. Divide the mousse mixture evenly into 4 individual serving glasses or ramekins. Refrigerate for at least 3-4 hours, or preferably overnight, until the mousse is firmly set. Serve chilled, optionally garnished with a few fresh berries.

title: Healthy Cinnamon Raisin Oatmeal Cookies

title: Healthy Spiced Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
ingredients_json: ["200 g Oats, rolled", "100 g Flour, whole wheat", "1 piece Egg, raw", "80 ml Maple syrup", "60 g Coconut oil, unrefined, melted", "120 g Applesauce, unsweetened", "1 tsp Baking soda", "0.5 tsp Salt, table", "1 tsp Cinnamon, ground", "0.5 tsp Vanilla extract", "70 g Raisins, dried"]

title: Light Berry & Greek Yogurt Pavlova with Fresh Mint

title: Berry and Greek Yogurt Mini Pavlovas

title: Berry Coconut Pavlova with Greek Yogurt Cream

title: Summer Berry and Greek Yogurt Mini Pavlovas

title: Healthy Flourless Maple Peanut Butter Cookies

title: Wholesome Oat & Peanut Butter Cookies

title: Wholesome Maple Peanut Butter Cookies

title: Maple-Kissed Pecan Pie with Whole Wheat Crust

title: Lemon Blueberry Greek Yogurt Pound Cake

instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a medium bowl, thoroughly mash the ripe bananas until they are smooth and creamy. Add the rolled oats, 60g of peanut butter, 30ml of maple syrup, vanilla extract, baking powder, and 1g of salt to the mashed bananas. Mix all ingredients well until a thick, uniform dough forms. Drop spoonfuls of the dough onto the prepared baking sheet, then flatten each portion gently into a circular cookie shape, approximately 5-6 cm in diameter. Bake the cookies for 12-15 minutes, or until their edges are golden brown and the cookies are set through. Allow the baked cookies to cool completely on a wire rack. While the cookies are cooling, prepare the creamy filling. In a small separate bowl, combine the remaining 80g of peanut butter, 15ml of maple syrup, and the unsweetened almond drink. Stir diligently until the mixture is smooth, fluffy, and well combined. Once the cookies are entirely cool, spread a generous amount of the peanut butter filling onto the flat side of half of the cookies. Gently top with the remaining cookies to create delightful sandwich cookies. Serve these healthy treats immediately or store them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

title: Healthy Oat Banana Sandwich Cookies with Peanut Butter Yogurt Filling
ingredients_json: ["200 g Banana, ripe", "1 piece Egg, raw", "100 g Oats, rolled, whole grain", "50 g Flour, whole wheat", "5 g Baking powder", "2 g Cinnamon, ground", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "10 g Maple syrup", "1 g Salt, table", "100 g Peanut butter, natural, unsalted", "50 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "10 g Maple syrup"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a large bowl, mash the ripe bananas thoroughly until smooth. Crack in the egg and mix well. Drop spoonfuls of the cookie dough onto the prepared baking sheet, flattening them slightly into small, uniform circles. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the cookies are firm to the touch. Carefully transfer the cookies to a wire rack to cool completely. While the cookies cool, prepare the filling: In a small bowl, combine the natural peanut butter, plain Greek yogurt, and the remaining 10 g maple syrup. Stir until the mixture is smooth and creamy. Once the cookies are entirely cool, spread a generous amount of the peanut butter yogurt filling onto the flat side of one cookie and gently press another cookie on top to create a sandwich. Repeat with the remaining cookies and filling, then serve.

title: Healthy Oatmeal Banana Sandwich Cookies with Peanut Butter Cream
ingredients_json: ["150 g Rolled oats, uncooked", "50 g Whole wheat flour", "2 medium Banana, ripe, about 200g", "50 ml Maple syrup, pure", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "5 g Baking powder", "2 g Cinnamon, ground", "100 g Peanut butter, natural, unsweetened", "30 ml Water", "15 ml Maple syrup, pure"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a food processor, pulse the rolled oats until they form a fine flour, then transfer to a large mixing bowl. Stir in 50 ml of maple syrup and the vanilla extract into the mashed bananas. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined, being careful not to overmix. Drop tablespoon-sized portions of the cookie dough onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them a couple of centimeters apart. Flatten them slightly with the back of a spoon to form round disks. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the cookies are set. Let the cookies cool completely on a wire rack before assembling. Once the cookies are cooled, spread a generous amount of the peanut butter cream onto the flat side of one cookie and top with another cookie to form a sandwich. Repeat with the remaining cookies.

title: Lemon & Almond Wholemeal Shortbread
ingredients_json: ["150 g Wheat flour, wholemeal", "50 g Almond flour", "80 g Butter, unsalted", "40 g Sugar, caster", "1 pc Lemon, zest of", "1 ml Vanilla extract", "1 g Salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). In a large mixing bowl, cream together the softened unsalted butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy. Stir in the lemon zest and vanilla extract, ensuring they are well incorporated. In a separate bowl, whisk together the wholemeal flour, almond flour, and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture, mixing until a soft dough forms. Avoid overworking the dough to keep the shortbread tender. Gather the dough into a ball, flatten it slightly, and wrap it in cling film. Chill the dough in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to firm up. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled dough to about 1 cm (1/2 inch) thickness. Cut the dough into desired shapes, such as squares, rounds, or traditional fingers. Place the cut shortbread pieces onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the shortbread is firm. The shortbread should still be pale in the center. Allow to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Whole Wheat Lemon Rosemary Shortbread
ingredients_json: ["180 g Whole wheat flour", "100 g Unsalted butter, cold", "20 g Granulated sugar", "15 ml Maple syrup", "1 tsp Lemon zest, fresh", "0.5 tsp Rosemary, fresh, finely chopped", "3 g Salt, table"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Line an 8x8 inch (20x20 cm) square baking tin with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides for easy removal. In a large bowl, combine the whole wheat flour and salt. Cut the cold butter into small cubes and add it to the flour mixture. Using your fingertips, rub the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Stir in the granulated sugar, maple syrup, fresh lemon zest, and finely chopped rosemary until just combined. Be careful not to overmix. Press the dough evenly into the prepared baking tin. You can score the top with a fork for a classic shortbread look. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the shortbread is firm to the touch. Remove from the oven and, while still warm, carefully cut into 12 squares or fingers. Allow to cool completely in the tin before removing and serving.

title: Lemon-Rosemary Whole Wheat Shortbread
ingredients_json: ["150 g Flour, wheat, whole grain", "100 g Flour, wheat, enriched, all-purpose", "120 g Butter, unsalted", "50 g Sugar, granulated", "1 piece Lemon, zest of", "1 sprig Rosemary, fresh, leaves finely chopped", "2 g Salt, table"]
instructions: In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy. Stir in the lemon zest, finely chopped fresh rosemary, and salt until well combined. Gradually add the whole wheat flour and all-purpose flour to the butter mixture, mixing on low speed or by hand until a cohesive dough forms. Be careful not to overmix. Gather the dough into a disc, wrap it in plastic film, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Preheat your oven to 160 degrees Celsius. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled dough to about 1 cm thickness. Cut into desired shapes (fingers, rounds, or squares) and arrange on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the shortbread is firm. Let the shortbread cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Lemon & Almond Wholemeal Shortbread
ingredients_json: ["140 g Wheat flour, wholemeal", "60 g Almond flour", "70 g Butter, unsalted", "25 g Maple syrup", "1 piece Lemon, zest", "1 g Salt"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). In a large bowl, combine the wholemeal wheat flour, almond flour, and salt. Grate the zest from one lemon directly into the flour mixture, ensuring to avoid the white pith. Add the softened unsalted butter and maple syrup to the bowl. Using your fingertips or a stand mixer with a paddle attachment, mix the ingredients until they come together to form a cohesive dough. Avoid overworking the dough to keep the shortbread tender. Press the dough evenly into an 18-20 cm (7-8 inch) round baking tin or a small square pan. Prick the surface all over with a fork to prevent it from puffing up. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the shortbread is firm to the touch. Remove from the oven and let it cool in the tin for about 10 minutes before carefully transferring it to a wire rack to cool completely. Once cooled, cut into 8 wedges or squares and serve.

title: Lemon & Rosemary Wholemeal Shortbread
ingredients_json: ["180 g Flour, whole wheat", "100 g Butter, unsalted, 80% fat", "50 g Sugar, granulated", "1 piece Lemon zest (from 1 medium lemon)", "1 tbsp Rosemary, fresh, chopped", "3 g Salt, table"]

Gradually add the whole wheat flour, mixing until the dough just comes together. Be careful not to overmix. Gently gather the dough and press it into a round disc, about 1 cm thick, on the prepared baking tray. Alternatively, you can press it into a 20 cm (8-inch) round cake pan. Prick the surface of the dough all over with a fork to prevent it from puffing up, and score it into 10 wedges, but do not cut all the way through. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the shortbread is lightly golden brown around the edges. Remove from the oven and, while still warm, carefully re-cut along the scored lines. Let it cool completely on the baking tray before separating the wedges.

title: Whole Wheat Strawberry Shortcakes with Vanilla Greek Yogurt Cream
ingredients_json: ["200 g Whole wheat flour", "15 g Granulated sugar", "10 g Baking powder", "2 g Salt", "50 g Butter, unsalted, cold", "120 ml Milk, low-fat, 1.5% fat", "400 g Strawberries, fresh", "15 g Maple syrup", "200 g Yogurt, Greek, plain, 0% fat", "2 ml Vanilla extract"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt until well combined. Cut the cold, unsalted butter into small pieces and add it to the dry ingredients. Use your fingertips or a pastry blender to work the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually pour in the low-fat milk, mixing gently with a spoon or your hands until just combined to form a soft dough. Be careful not to overmix, as this can lead to tough shortcakes. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and gently pat or roll it to an even thickness of about 2 centimeters. Using a round cookie cutter (approximately 6-7 cm in diameter), cut out 6 shortcakes. Place the shortcakes on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving a small space between each. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the tops are golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. While the shortcakes are baking, prepare the strawberries and yogurt topping. Wash and hull the fresh strawberries, then slice them into bite-sized pieces. In a medium bowl, gently toss the sliced strawberries with the maple syrup, allowing them to macerate slightly. In a separate small bowl, combine the Greek yogurt with the vanilla extract and stir until smooth. Once the shortcakes are baked, transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely. To serve, carefully split each cooled shortcake in half horizontally using a serrated knife. Spoon a generous portion of the macerated strawberries onto the bottom half of each shortcake, then add a dollop of the vanilla Greek yogurt cream. Place the top half of the shortcake on top and serve immediately for the best texture and flavor.

title: Strawberry Basil Shortcakes with Greek Yogurt Cream
ingredients_json: ["250 g Whole wheat flour", "10 g Baking powder", "2 g Salt", "15 g Granulated sugar", "50 g Cold butter, unsalted", "120 ml Plain yogurt, low-fat", "500 g Strawberries, fresh", "10 g Granulated sugar", "1 tsp Fresh basil, chopped", "250 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "10 g Granulated sugar", "1 tsp Vanilla extract"]
instructions:
Preheat your oven to 200 degrees Celsius. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, baking powder, salt, and 15 grams of granulated sugar. Cut the cold butter into small cubes and add it to the flour mixture. Use your fingertips or a pastry blender to cut the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add the low-fat plain yogurt, mixing just until the dough comes together. Be careful not to overmix. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and gently pat it into a round or rectangle about 2 cm thick. Using a 6-7 cm round cutter, cut out 6 shortcakes. Place the shortcakes on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. Let them cool on a wire rack.
While the shortcakes cool, prepare the strawberries and cream. Wash and hull the fresh strawberries, then slice or quarter them. In a medium bowl, gently toss the strawberries with 10 grams of granulated sugar and the chopped fresh basil. Set aside to macerate for at least 10 minutes. In another bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, 10 grams of granulated sugar, and vanilla extract, stirring until well combined and smooth.
To assemble, slice each cooled shortcake horizontally. Place the bottom half on a serving plate, spoon a generous amount of the macerated strawberries over it, then add a dollop of the Greek yogurt cream. Top with the other half of the shortcake and serve immediately.

title: Whole Wheat Strawberry and Greek Yogurt Shortcakes

title: Healthy Whole Wheat Snickerdoodles with Maple
ingredients_json: ["200 g Whole wheat pastry flour", "100 g Unsalted butter, softened", "100 g Coconut sugar", "50 g Maple syrup", "1 piece Egg, large, raw", "2 tsp Cream of tartar", "1 tsp Baking soda", "0.5 tsp Salt, table", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "2 tbsp Coconut sugar, for coating", "1 tbsp Ground cinnamon, for coating"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. In a medium bowl, whisk together the whole wheat pastry flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, and salt until well combined. Set this dry mixture aside. In a large mixing bowl, using an electric mixer, cream together the softened unsalted butter, 100g of coconut sugar, and maple syrup until the mixture is light and fluffy, usually about 2-3 minutes. Beat in the large egg and vanilla extract until they are fully incorporated and the mixture is smooth. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing on low speed until a soft, pliable dough forms. Be careful not to overmix the dough. In a small, shallow bowl, combine the remaining 2 tablespoons of coconut sugar and 1 tablespoon of ground cinnamon for the coating. Scoop out the dough, approximately 1.5 tablespoons per cookie, and roll it into uniform balls. Roll each dough ball thoroughly in the cinnamon-sugar mixture, ensuring an even and complete coating. Place the coated dough balls about 5 cm (2 inches) apart on the prepared baking sheets. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and set, but the centers still appear slightly soft. The cookies will firm up more as they cool. Remove the baking sheets from the oven and let the cookies cool on the sheets for a few minutes before carefully transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Whole Wheat Lemon-Kissed Snickerdoodles with Applesauce
ingredients_json: ["250 g Whole wheat flour, fine ground", "60 g Butter, unsalted", "40 g Applesauce, unsweetened", "100 g Cane sugar, white", "1 piece Egg, raw (approx. 50g)", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "5 g Cream of tartar", "3 g Baking soda", "1 g Salt, table", "5 ml Lemon juice, fresh", "20 g Cane sugar, white (for coating)", "5 g Cinnamon, ground (for coating)"]

The cookies will puff up and then flatten slightly as they cool. Let them cool on the baking sheet for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Whole Wheat Snickerdoodles with Reduced Sugar

title: Healthy Whole Wheat Apple Ginger Spice Cake
ingredients_json: ["200 g Whole wheat flour", "100 g All-purpose flour, white", "2 tsp Baking powder", "1 tsp Baking soda", "1 tsp Ground cinnamon", "1 tsp Ground ginger", "0.5 tsp Ground nutmeg", "0.25 tsp Ground cloves", "0.5 tsp Salt, table", "2 piece Egg, raw, whole", "150 ml Maple syrup", "60 ml Olive oil", "120 ml Apple sauce, unsweetened", "120 ml Milk, low-fat, 1.5% fat", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "200 g Apple, fresh, with skin, grated", "50 g Walnuts, chopped"]

ingredients_json: ["250 g Whole wheat pastry flour", "50 g Wheat flour, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached", "90 g Butter, unsalted", "70 g Granulated sugar", "30 g Erythritol, crystalline", "1 piece Egg, raw, whole, large", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "5 g Baking powder", "2 g Salt, table"]
instructions: In a large bowl, cream together the softened unsalted butter, granulated sugar, and erythritol until light and fluffy. Beat in the large egg and vanilla extract until well combined. In a separate bowl, whisk together the whole wheat pastry flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined and a soft dough forms. Be careful not to overmix. Divide the dough into two flattened discs, wrap them tightly in plastic wrap, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, or up to 24 hours. Preheat your oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit) and line baking sheets with parchment paper. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one disc of chilled dough to about 5 mm (1/4 inch) thickness. Use cookie cutters to cut out desired shapes and carefully transfer them to the prepared baking sheets. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden. Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

title: Healthy Spiced Sweet Potato Pie with Whole Wheat Crust
ingredients_json: ["200 g Wheat flour, whole grain", "100 g Butter, unsalted, cold", "50 ml Water, ice cold", "2 g Salt", "700 g Sweet potato, cooked, mashed", "2 pieces Egg, raw, large", "100 ml Milk, low fat (1.5% fat)", "80 ml Maple syrup, pure", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "5 g Cinnamon, ground", "2 g Nutmeg, ground", "1 g Ginger, ground", "1 g Allspice, ground"]
instructions: To prepare the crust, combine the whole wheat flour and 1 gram of salt in a large bowl. Cut the cold unsalted butter into small cubes and add to the flour mixture. Using your fingertips, a pastry blender, or a food processor, cut the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter remaining. Gradually add the ice-cold water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Be careful not to overmix. Form the dough into a disc, wrap it in plastic film, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled pie dough into a 30 cm (12-inch) circle. Carefully transfer the dough to a 23 cm (9-inch) pie dish. Trim and crimp the edges as desired. To make the filling, in a large bowl, whisk together the mashed sweet potato, eggs, low-fat milk, maple syrup, vanilla extract, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, allspice, and the remaining 1 gram of salt until smooth and well combined. Pour the sweet potato filling into the prepared pie crust. Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until the center is just set and the crust is golden brown. A knife inserted near the center should come out mostly clean. If the crust edges start to brown too quickly, you can cover them loosely with aluminum foil. Let the pie cool completely on a wire rack before slicing and serving. This allows the filling to fully set.

title: Healthy Spiced Sweet Potato Pie with Almond-Oat Crust
ingredients_json: ["150 g Whole wheat flour", "50 g Rolled oats", "30 g Almond flour", "70 g Butter, unsalted, cold", "60 ml Water, ice cold", "2 g Salt, table", "700 g Sweet potato, raw, skin on", "2 piece Egg, raw, whole", "200 ml Coconut milk, light, canned", "80 ml Maple syrup", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "5 g Cinnamon, ground", "2 g Nutmeg, ground", "2 g Ginger, ground", "1 g Salt, table"]

Gradually add the ice water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Form the dough into a disc, wrap it in cling film, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Meanwhile, preheat your oven to 190°C. To prepare the sweet potatoes, peel and cube them. Steam or boil them until very tender, about 15-20 minutes, then drain well and let them cool slightly. For the filling, in a large bowl, mash the cooked sweet potatoes until smooth. Add the eggs, light coconut milk, maple syrup, vanilla extract, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and 1 gram of salt. Bake the pie for 50-60 minutes, or until the edges of the crust are golden brown and the filling is set; a knife inserted into the center should come out clean. title: Spiced Sweet Potato Pie with Whole Wheat Crust
ingredients_json: ["200 g Whole wheat flour", "60 g Cold butter, unsalted", "60 ml Cold water", "2 g Salt, table", "800 g Sweet potato, raw", "2 piece Egg, raw", "150 ml Milk, low fat, 1.5% fat", "100 g Maple syrup", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "5 g Cinnamon, ground", "2 g Nutmeg, ground", "1 g Ginger, ground"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F). For the pie crust, in a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour and salt. Gradually add the cold water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. While the crust chills or bakes, prepare the filling. Peel and cut the sweet potatoes into chunks, then boil or steam them until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. In a large mixing bowl, combine the mashed sweet potato, eggs, low-fat milk, maple syrup, vanilla extract, ground cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger. title: Wholesome Spiced Sweet Potato Pie with Whole Wheat Crust
ingredients_json: ["800 g Sweet potato, raw, unspecified", "200 g Wheat flour, whole grain, unspecified", "50 g Butter, unsalted", "60 ml Water, tap", "2 piece Egg, raw", "200 ml Milk, low fat, unspecified", "100 g Maple syrup", "5 g Cinnamon, ground", "2 g Nutmeg, ground", "1 g Ginger, ground", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "2 g Salt, table"]
instructions: First, prepare the pie crust. In a large bowl, combine the whole wheat flour and a pinch of salt. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add the cold water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until a dough forms. Do not overmix. Gather the dough into a ball, flatten slightly, wrap in cling film, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Meanwhile, preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into chunks. Steam or boil them until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well and mash them thoroughly with a fork or potato masher until smooth. In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, low-fat milk, maple syrup, ground cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and vanilla extract until well combined. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the chilled pie dough into a circle large enough to fit a 23 cm (9-inch) pie dish. Carefully transfer the dough to the pie dish, trimming and crimping the edges as desired. Pour the sweet potato filling into the prepared crust. Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until the filling is set and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean. If the crust begins to brown too quickly, you can cover the edges with foil. Let the pie cool completely on a wire rack before slicing and serving.

title: Maple-Kissed Sweet Potato Pie with Spiced Whole Wheat Crust
ingredients_json: ["150 g Whole wheat flour", "50 g Oat flour", "2 g Salt, fine", "70 g Butter, unsalted, cold", "60 ml Water, cold, ice", "900 g Sweet potato, raw", "2 pieces Egg, large, raw", "250 ml Almond milk, unsweetened", "80 ml Maple syrup, pure", "30 g Brown sugar, light", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "5 g Cinnamon, ground", "2 g Nutmeg, ground", "1 g Ginger, ground", "0.5 g Cloves, ground"]
instructions:
To prepare the crust, whisk together the whole wheat flour, oat flour, and 1 gram of salt in a large bowl. Cut the cold butter into small cubes and use a pastry blender or your fingertips to work the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add the ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough just comes together. Form the dough into a disk, wrap it in cling film, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Once chilled, roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface to a 30 cm circle and carefully transfer it to a 23 cm pie dish. Trim and crimp the edges, then prick the bottom with a fork several times. Preheat your oven to 190°C. Bake the pie crust for 10-12 minutes, or until lightly golden. Remove from oven and let cool slightly.
For the filling, pierce the sweet potatoes several times with a fork and bake them at 200°C for 45-60 minutes, or until very tender. Alternatively, boil them until soft. Scoop out the flesh and mash it until completely smooth, ensuring there are no lumps; you should have approximately 700 grams of mashed sweet potato. In a separate large bowl, whisk together the eggs, almond milk, maple syrup, brown sugar, vanilla extract, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and the remaining 1 gram of salt until well combined. title: Lightened Espresso Tiramisu with Greek Yogurt
ingredients_json: ["150 g Ladyfingers, light", "3 dl Espresso, unsweetened, cooled", "250 g Mascarpone cheese, light", "200 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "1 piece Egg yolk, raw, large", "3 pieces Egg white, raw, large", "30 g Cane sugar, granulated", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "15 g Cocoa powder, unsweetened"]
instructions: First, prepare a strong espresso and allow it to cool completely. In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolk with half of the cane sugar until light and creamy. Gently fold in the light mascarpone cheese and Greek yogurt until the mixture is smooth and well combined. In a separate, clean bowl, whisk the egg whites with the remaining cane sugar and vanilla extract until stiff peaks form. Carefully fold the egg white mixture into the mascarpone and yogurt mixture in several additions, ensuring to keep as much air as possible in the cream. Briefly dip each ladyfinger into the cooled espresso, making sure not to over-soak them, and arrange a single layer at the bottom of a serving dish. Spread half of the cream mixture evenly over the ladyfingers. Repeat with another layer of espresso-dipped ladyfingers, followed by the remaining cream. Cover the dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld and the tiramisu to set. Before serving, dust generously with unsweetened cocoa powder.

title: Healthier Espresso Tiramisu with Greek Yogurt
ingredients_json: ["350 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "200 g Mascarpone, light", "3 pieces Egg, raw, large", "50 g Erythritol, powdered", "2.5 dl Espresso, brewed, strong, unsweetened", "150 g Ladyfingers, whole grain", "2 tsp Vanilla extract", "15 g Cocoa powder, unsweetened"]
instructions: First, separate the egg yolks from the whites. In a large bowl, whisk the egg yolks with the erythritol until pale and creamy. Gently fold in the light mascarpone and Greek yogurt until well combined and smooth, then add the vanilla extract. In a separate, clean bowl, whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form. Carefully fold the whipped egg whites into the yogurt-mascarpone mixture in two additions, being careful not to deflate the mixture. Brew strong espresso and let it cool completely. Dip each whole grain ladyfinger briefly into the cooled espresso; do not over-soak, as they can become soggy. Arrange a single layer of soaked ladyfingers at the bottom of a serving dish. Spread half of the yogurt-mascarpone cream over the ladyfingers. Repeat with another layer of espresso-dipped ladyfingers and the remaining cream. Cover the dish and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld and the tiramisu to set. Just before serving, dust generously with unsweetened cocoa powder.

title: Healthy Date and Almond Toffee Bark
ingredients_json: ["200 g Dates, pitted, Medjool", "100 g Almonds, raw, unsalted", "30 ml Coconut oil, virgin", "30 ml Maple syrup, pure", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "1 g Sea salt", "50 g Chocolate, dark, 70-85% cocoa"]
instructions: Line a small baking sheet (approximately 20x20 cm) with parchment paper, ensuring an overhang on the sides for easy removal later. In a food processor, combine the pitted dates, raw almonds, coconut oil, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and sea salt. Process on high until the mixture forms a thick, sticky dough that comes together and pulls away from the sides of the bowl. If the mixture appears too dry, add an additional 5 ml of coconut oil or a teaspoon of water, one at a time, until the desired consistency is achieved. Evenly press the date-almond mixture into the prepared baking sheet, spreading it out to an even thickness of about 1 cm. Use the back of a spoon or your hands to flatten it smooth. Melt the dark chocolate in a microwave-safe bowl in 30-second intervals, stirring thoroughly between each, or melt it over a double boiler until smooth and completely liquid. Pour the melted dark chocolate evenly over the date-almond base, then use an offset spatula to spread it smoothly to the edges. Place the baking sheet in the refrigerator for at least 1-2 hours, or until the toffee bark is firm and the chocolate has set completely. Once firm, lift the parchment paper from the baking sheet and transfer the bark to a cutting board. Cut the bark into approximately 12 squares or irregular shards using a sharp knife. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator to maintain freshness.

title: Healthy Date and Almond Toffee Bites
ingredients_json: ["200 g Dates, Medjool, pitted", "100 g Almonds, raw, unsalted", "2 tbsp Coconut oil, virgin", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "0.5 tsp Sea salt, fine"]
instructions: Place the pitted Medjool dates, raw almonds, virgin coconut oil, vanilla extract, and sea salt into a high-speed food processor. Process until the mixture forms a sticky, uniform dough that comes together when pressed. It should resemble a thick, crumbly paste. Line an 8x8 inch (20x20 cm) baking dish with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides for easy removal. Press the toffee mixture evenly and firmly into the prepared dish, ensuring it is compact and smooth on top. Place the dish in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until the toffee is firm enough to cut. Once firm, lift the toffee slab out of the dish using the parchment paper and cut it into small, bite-sized squares or rectangles. Store the toffee bites in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

title: No-Bake Date & Almond Toffee Bites
ingredients_json: ["200 g Dates, Medjool, pitted", "100 g Almonds, raw, unsalted", "50 g Oats, rolled", "30 ml Maple syrup, pure", "15 ml Coconut oil, virgin", "2 ml Vanilla extract", "1 g Salt, fine"]
instructions: Line a 20x20 cm baking dish with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides for easy removal. In a food processor, combine the raw almonds and rolled oats. Pulse until they form a coarse flour-like consistency, being careful not to over-process into butter. Add the pitted Medjool dates, maple syrup, virgin coconut oil, vanilla extract, and fine salt to the food processor. Process the mixture on high speed until a sticky, cohesive dough forms. It should stick together when pressed between your fingers. Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish. Press the mixture down firmly and evenly using the back of a spoon or your hands, ensuring it is compact and flat. Place the dish in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until the toffee bites are firm enough to cut. Once firm, use the parchment paper overhang to lift the slab from the dish and place it on a cutting board. Cut into approximately 16-20 small squares. Store the toffee bites in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

title: Chewy Almond & Date Toffee Bites with Dark Chocolate Drizzle
ingredients_json: ["250 g Medjool dates, pitted", "120 g Almond butter, unsweetened", "50 g Rolled oats, whole grain", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "2 g Sea salt", "50 g Almonds, toasted and roughly chopped", "30 g Dark chocolate, minimum 70% cocoa solids"]
instructions: Line a small square baking dish (approximately 20x20 cm) with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides for easy removal. Place the pitted Medjool dates into a food processor and process until they form a sticky paste. It may take a few minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed. Add the almond butter, rolled oats, vanilla extract, and sea salt to the date paste in the food processor. Process again until all ingredients are well combined and the mixture forms a uniform dough. Stir in the chopped toasted almonds by hand or pulse briefly in the food processor to incorporate without over-processing. Press the mixture firmly and evenly into the prepared baking dish. If desired, melt the dark chocolate in a microwave-safe bowl in 30-second intervals, stirring in between, or over a double boiler. Drizzle the melted dark chocolate evenly over the pressed toffee mixture. Place the dish in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until the toffee is firm enough to cut. Once set, lift the toffee out of the dish using the parchment paper overhang and cut into 12 even squares or bars. Store the toffee bites in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

title: Lemon Raspberry Almond Torte
ingredients_json: ["200 g Almond flour, blanched", "50 g Whole wheat flour, fine", "3 pieces Egg, large, raw", "100 ml Maple syrup, pure", "150 g Greek yogurt, 0% fat", "200 g Raspberries, fresh", "1 piece Lemon, medium", "10 g Baking powder", "5 ml Vanilla extract, pure", "1 g Salt, table", "10 ml Olive oil, extra virgin"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175 degrees Celsius. Lightly grease a 22 cm springform pan with olive oil and dust with a little almond flour to prevent sticking. In a large bowl, whisk together the almond flour, whole wheat flour, baking powder, and salt. In a separate medium bowl, whisk the eggs, maple syrup, Greek yogurt, the zest and juice of the lemon, and vanilla extract until well combined. Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, mixing gently until just combined. Be careful not to overmix. Gently fold in 150 grams of the fresh raspberries. Pour the batter into the prepared springform pan, spreading evenly. Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean and the top is golden brown. If the top browns too quickly, you can loosely tent it with foil. Let the torte cool completely in the pan on a wire rack before carefully removing the sides. Garnish with the remaining 50 grams of fresh raspberries before serving.

title: Healthy Dark Chocolate Berry Almond Torte
ingredients_json: ["200 g Almond flour", "70 g Dates, dried, pitted", "20 g Cocoa powder, unsweetened", "30 ml Water", "1 g Salt, fine", "150 g Dark chocolate, 70-85% cocoa solids", "100 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "2 pieces Egg, raw, large", "50 g Erythritol, granular", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "100 g Raspberries, fresh", "50 g Raspberries, fresh, for garnish", "5 g Mint, fresh leaves"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175 degrees Celsius. Lightly grease and line the bottom of a 20 cm springform pan with parchment paper. To prepare the crust, combine the almond flour, pitted dates, cocoa powder, and salt in a food processor. Process until the dates are finely chopped and the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add the water gradually while processing until the mixture starts to clump together. Press this mixture evenly into the bottom of the prepared springform pan. For the filling, gently melt the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water, ensuring the bowl does not touch the water, or use a microwave in short bursts. Allow it to cool slightly. In a separate large bowl, whisk together the eggs, erythritol, and vanilla extract until light and fluffy. Fold in the Greek yogurt until just combined, then gently incorporate the slightly cooled melted dark chocolate. Stir in the 100 g of fresh raspberries carefully to avoid crushing them too much. Pour the chocolate-raspberry filling over the almond crust in the springform pan. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the edges are set but the center still has a slight jiggle. Remove from the oven and let it cool completely on a wire rack before refrigerating for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow it to set firmly. Once chilled, carefully remove the torte from the springform pan. Garnish with the remaining 50 g of fresh raspberries and fresh mint leaves before serving.

title: Spiced Apple and Almond Flour Torte
ingredients_json: ["150 g Almond flour, blanched", "50 g Rolled oats, gluten-free", "30 g Erythritol, granular", "60 g Butter, unsalted, melted", "1 tsp Cinnamon, ground", "300 g Apple, fresh, peeled, cored and diced", "2 pieces Egg, raw, large", "100 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "50 g Erythritol, granular", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "0.5 tsp Nutmeg, ground", "0.25 tsp Cardamom, ground", "1 tbsp Lemon juice, fresh", "20 g Sliced almonds", "10 g Erythritol, powdered (for dusting)"]

Press this mixture firmly into the bottom of the prepared springform pan to form an even crust. Bake the crust for 10-12 minutes, or until lightly golden, then remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly. While the crust bakes, prepare the apple filling. In a separate large bowl, whisk together the eggs, Greek yogurt, the remaining 50g of granular erythritol, vanilla extract, nutmeg, cardamom, and lemon juice until well combined. Gently fold in the diced apples. Pour the apple filling evenly over the partially baked crust. Sprinkle the sliced almonds over the top of the torte. Return the torte to the oven and bake for 45-55 minutes, or until the center is set and the top is golden brown. A knife inserted into the center should come out mostly clean. Let the torte cool completely on a wire rack before carefully removing it from the springform pan. Dust with powdered erythritol before serving.

title: Lemon Raspberry Almond Torte
ingredients_json: ["150 g Almond flour", "50 g Rolled oats", "45 g Coconut oil, unrefined, melted", "30 ml Maple syrup", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "1 g Salt, fine", "250 g Cream cheese, light", "200 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "2 piece Egg, raw, whole", "60 ml Lemon juice, fresh", "5 g Lemon zest", "50 ml Maple syrup", "15 g Corn starch", "200 g Raspberries, fresh"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C (350°F). Lightly grease a 23 cm (9-inch) springform pan and line the bottom with parchment paper. For the crust, pulse the rolled oats in a food processor until they resemble a coarse flour, then add the almond flour, melted coconut oil, 30 ml maple syrup, vanilla extract, and salt. Process until the mixture comes together. Press this mixture evenly into the bottom of the prepared springform pan. Bake the crust for 10-12 minutes, or until lightly golden. While the crust is baking, prepare the filling. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the light cream cheese until smooth. Add the Greek yogurt, eggs, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, 50 ml maple syrup, and corn starch. Beat until the mixture is well combined and smooth, scraping down the sides of the bowl as needed. Gently fold in the fresh raspberries. Pour the filling over the partially baked crust. Return the torte to the oven and bake for 45-55 minutes, or until the edges are set and the center jiggles only slightly when gently shaken. Turn off the oven, crack the door open slightly, and let the torte cool in the oven for about 1 hour. This helps prevent cracking. Remove the torte from the oven and let it cool completely on a wire rack before refrigerating for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow it to fully set. Before serving, carefully remove the sides of the springform pan.

title: Lemon Blueberry Almond Torte
ingredients_json: ["150 g Almond flour", "50 g Whole wheat flour", "50 g Butter, unsalted, melted", "30 ml Maple syrup", "1 g Salt", "250 g Cream cheese, light", "2 pieces Egg, raw, large", "50 g Cane sugar", "1 tsp Vanilla extract", "1 piece Lemon, fresh (for zest)", "30 ml Lemon juice, fresh", "200 g Blueberries, fresh or frozen", "1 tbsp Corn starch"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly grease and flour a 20 cm (8-inch) springform pan, then set aside. For the crust, in a medium bowl, combine the almond flour, whole wheat flour, melted unsalted butter, maple syrup, and salt, mixing until crumbs form and can be pressed together. Press this mixture evenly into the bottom of the prepared springform pan. Bake the crust for 10 minutes until it's lightly golden, then remove it from the oven and allow it to cool slightly while you prepare the filling. For the filling, in a large bowl, beat the light cream cheese with an electric mixer until it is smooth and creamy. Add the large eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition to ensure everything is fully incorporated. Stir in the cane sugar, vanilla extract, grated lemon zest from one lemon, and fresh lemon juice until the mixture is uniform. In a separate small bowl, gently toss the fresh or frozen blueberries with the corn starch, making sure they are evenly coated. Pour about half of the cream cheese filling mixture over the cooled crust in the springform pan. Carefully sprinkle half of the corn starch-coated blueberries over this layer. Pour the remaining cream cheese mixture over the blueberries, then evenly top with the rest of the blueberries. Bake the torte for 45-55 minutes, or until the edges are set and the center jiggles only slightly when gently shaken. To prevent cracking, turn off the oven, crack the door open slightly, and let the torte cool in the oven for an additional 30 minutes. Remove the torte from the oven and place it on a wire rack to cool completely to room temperature. Once cooled, chill the torte in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, before carefully removing it from the springform pan and slicing to serve.

title: Dark Chocolate Almond Date Truffles
ingredients_json: ["200 g Medjool dates, pitted", "60 g Almond butter, unsweetened", "30 g Cacao powder, unsweetened", "15 g Chia seeds", "1 tbsp Vanilla extract", "0.5 g Sea salt", "10 g Cacao powder, unsweetened (for coating)"]
instructions: In a food processor, combine the pitted Medjool dates, unsweetened almond butter, 30 grams of cacao powder, chia seeds, vanilla extract, and sea salt. Process until a sticky, uniform dough forms. Scrape down the sides as needed to ensure all ingredients are well combined. If the mixture appears too dry, you may add 1-2 teaspoons of water to achieve a pliable consistency. Once smooth and cohesive, transfer the mixture from the food processor to a bowl. Roll the dough into small, bite-sized balls, aiming for approximately 20-25 grams each. Place the remaining 10 grams of cacao powder in a shallow dish. Roll each truffle in the cacao powder until it is evenly coated on all sides. Arrange the coated truffles on a plate or tray lined with parchment paper and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm up before serving.

title: Dark Chocolate Avocado Truffles with Toasted Almonds
ingredients_json: ["150 g Avocado, raw", "100 g Dark chocolate, 85% cacao", "30 g Maple syrup", "50 g Almond flour", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "1 g Salt, table", "10 g Cacao powder, unsweetened", "20 g Almonds, toasted, chopped"]
instructions: Begin by gently melting the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water, ensuring the bowl does not touch the water, or use a microwave in short bursts, stirring frequently. Once melted and smooth, set aside to cool slightly. In a food processor, combine the raw avocado, cooled melted dark chocolate, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and salt. Process until the mixture is completely smooth and creamy, scraping down the sides as needed to ensure no lumps remain. Add the almond flour to the food processor and pulse until just combined, forming a thick, uniform truffle mixture. Transfer the mixture to a bowl, cover it, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until it is firm enough to roll. Once firm, use a small spoon or scoop to portion out the mixture and roll it into small, bite-sized balls. In a shallow dish, combine the unsweetened cacao powder and the toasted, chopped almonds. Roll each truffle in this coating, pressing gently to ensure an even layer. Place the coated truffles back onto a plate or tray and refrigerate for another 30 minutes to set completely before serving.

title: Healthy Dark Chocolate Avocado Truffles
ingredients_json: ["150 g Dark chocolate, 70-85% cocoa solids", "120 g Avocado, ripe, peeled, pitted", "30 g Cocoa powder, unsweetened", "30 g Maple syrup", "5 g Vanilla extract", "2 g Sea salt, fine", "50 g Desiccated coconut, unsweetened", "20 g Cacao nibs"]
instructions: First, melt the dark chocolate. You can do this by placing it in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie method), stirring until smooth, or by microwaving in short bursts, stirring frequently. Once melted, set aside to cool slightly. In a food processor, combine the peeled and pitted avocado, unsweetened cocoa powder, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and sea salt. Process until completely smooth and creamy, ensuring there are no avocado lumps remaining. Pour the slightly cooled melted chocolate into the food processor with the avocado mixture. Process again until well combined and the mixture is uniformly dark and smooth. Scrape the mixture into a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until firm enough to roll. While the truffle mixture chills, prepare your coatings: place the desiccated coconut on one small plate and the cacao nibs on another. Once chilled, scoop out small portions of the truffle mixture (about 15-20g each) and roll them between your palms to form smooth balls. Roll each truffle in your chosen coating, ensuring it is fully covered. Place the finished truffles on a parchment-lined tray and refrigerate until ready to serve. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

title: Healthy Apple and Oat Upside-Down Cake with Cinnamon
ingredients_json: ["2 piece Apple, Red, raw (medium)", "30 g Maple syrup", "10 g Butter, unsalted", "2 g Cinnamon, ground (for topping)", "150 g Flour, whole wheat", "50 g Rolled oats, uncooked", "70 g Brown sugar, light", "1 piece Egg, raw, large", "150 ml Milk, semi-skimmed", "60 ml Rapeseed oil", "10 g Baking powder", "2 g Baking soda", "3 g Cinnamon, ground (for batter)", "3 ml Vanilla extract", "2 g Salt, table"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F) and lightly grease a 23 cm (9-inch) round cake pan. In a small microwave-safe bowl, melt the unsalted butter, then stir in the maple syrup and 2 grams of ground cinnamon. Pour this mixture evenly into the bottom of the prepared cake pan. Wash and core the apples, then slice them thinly and arrange them in a single layer over the syrup mixture in the pan. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, rolled oats, light brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 3 grams of ground cinnamon, and salt. In a separate medium bowl, whisk the large egg, semi-skimmed milk, rapeseed oil, and vanilla extract until well combined. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined; be careful not to overmix, as this can make the cake tough. Gently spoon the cake batter over the apple slices in the pan, spreading it evenly to cover them. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean. Let the cake cool in the pan on a wire rack for about 10 minutes. Then, carefully invert the cake onto a serving plate. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Healthy Pineapple-Ginger Whole Wheat Upside-Down Cake
ingredients_json: ["1 piece Pineapple, fresh (approx. 500g before peeling/coring)", "15 g Butter, unsalted", "45 ml Maple syrup", "1 g Ginger, ground", "180 g Flour, whole wheat", "60 g Oats, rolled, dry", "1.5 tsp Baking powder", "0.5 tsp Baking soda", "0.25 tsp Salt, table", "2 piece Egg, raw, large", "1.5 dl Yogurt, plain, low fat", "60 ml Maple syrup", "4 tbsp Olive oil", "5 ml Vanilla extract"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 175°C (350°F). Lightly grease an 8-inch round cake pan. Peel and core the fresh pineapple, then slice it into rings about 1 cm thick; pat them dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture. In a small saucepan over medium-low heat, melt the unsalted butter. Add the 45 ml of maple syrup and the ground ginger, stirring until well combined and slightly bubbly, about 1 minute. Pour this mixture evenly into the bottom of the prepared cake pan. Arrange the pineapple slices over the maple-ginger mixture in a single layer, making an appealing pattern. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, rolled oats, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. In a separate medium bowl, whisk the eggs, low-fat plain yogurt, the remaining 60 ml of maple syrup, olive oil, and vanilla extract until smooth. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix with a spatula until just combined; be careful not to overmix, as this can lead to a tough cake. Gently spoon the cake batter over the pineapple slices in the pan, spreading it evenly to cover them completely. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean. Let the cake cool in the pan on a wire rack for 10 minutes. Then, carefully place a serving plate over the cake pan and, using oven mitts, quickly invert the cake onto the plate. Remove the pan, allowing any caramelized topping to drizzle over the cake. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Healthy Pumpkin Spice Whoopie Pies with Light Cream Cheese Filling
ingredients_json: ["150 g Whole wheat pastry flour", "50 g Oat flour", "5 g Baking powder", "2 g Baking soda", "5 g Pumpkin pie spice blend", "2 g Salt, table", "200 g Pumpkin puree, canned, unsweetened", "80 ml Maple syrup, pure", "1 piece Egg, raw, large", "30 ml Coconut oil, refined, melted", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "150 g Cream cheese, light, 15% fat", "50 g Powdered sugar", "2 ml Vanilla extract"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180 degrees Celsius and line two baking sheets with parchment paper. In a large bowl, whisk together the whole wheat pastry flour, oat flour, baking powder, baking soda, pumpkin pie spice blend, and salt until well combined. In a separate medium bowl, combine the pumpkin puree, maple syrup, egg, melted coconut oil, and vanilla extract, mixing until smooth. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir gently until just combined, being careful not to overmix. Drop rounded tablespoons of the batter onto the prepared baking sheets, leaving some space between each dollop as they will spread slightly. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until the edges are set and the tops spring back when lightly touched. Allow the whoopie pie shells to cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. While the shells are cooling, prepare the filling: in a small bowl, beat the light cream cheese, powdered sugar, and vanilla extract together until smooth and creamy. Once the whoopie pie shells are completely cool, spread a generous amount of the cream cheese filling on the flat side of one shell and then top with another shell to create a sandwich. Repeat with the remaining shells and filling.

title: Spiced Pumpkin Whole Wheat Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Cream Cheese Filling

title: Spiced Pumpkin Whole Wheat Whoopie Pies with Greek Yogurt Cream
ingredients_json: ["180 g Whole wheat flour", "50 g All-purpose flour", "10 g Baking powder", "5 g Ground cinnamon", "2 g Ground nutmeg", "1 g Ground ginger", "1 g Salt", "90 g Butter, unsalted, softened", "100 g Brown sugar", "1 piece Egg, raw", "200 g Pumpkin puree, canned", "120 ml Milk, low-fat", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "200 g Greek yogurt, plain, 0% fat", "30 g Powdered sugar", "5 ml Vanilla extract", "40 g Cream cheese, light"]
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. In a medium bowl, whisk together the whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and salt until well combined. Beat in the egg until it is fully incorporated, then stir in the pumpkin puree and vanilla extract. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with the milk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients. Once the pie halves are completely cooled, spread about 1-2 tablespoons of the filling onto the flat side of one pie half and then gently top with another pie half, pressing them together lightly to form a sandwich. Repeat this process with the remaining pie halves and filling.
